children.translated_text: <s>Daśakumāracarita</s> (The Tale of the Ten Princes) — Third Chapter

children.text: eṣo 'smi paryaṭann ekadā gato videheṣu | mithilām apraviśyaiva bahiḥ kva=cin maṭhi kāyā viśramitum etya kayā api vṛddhatāpasyā dattapādyaḥ kṣaṇam alindabhūmāv avāsthiṣi | tasyās tu maddarśanād eva kim apy ābaddhadhāram aśru prāvartata | ' kim etad amba kathaya kāraṇam ' iti pṛṣṭā sakaruṇam ācaṣṭa  'jaivātṛka nanu śrūyate patir asyā mithilāyāḥ prahāravarmā nāmāsīt | tasya khalu magadharājo rājahamsaḥ paraṃ mitram āsīt | tayoś ca vallabhe balaśambalayor iva vasumatīpriyamvade sakhyam apratimam adhattām | atha prathamagarbhābhinanditāṃ tāṃ ca priyasakhīṃ didṛkṣuḥ priyamvadā vasumatīṃ saha bhartrā puṣpapuram agamat | tasminn eva ca samaye mālavena magadharājasya mahaj janyam ajani | tatra leśato 'pi durlakṣāṃ gatim agaman magadharājaḥ | maithilendras tu mālavendraprayatnaprāṇitaḥ svaviṣayaṃ prati nivṛtto jyeṣṭhasya samhāravarmaṇaḥ sutair vikaṭavarmaprabhṛtibhir vyāptaṃ rājyam ākarṇya svasrīyāt suhmapater daṇḍāvayavam āditsur aṭavīpatham avagāhya lubdhakaluptasarvasvo 'bhūt | tatsutena ca kanīyasā hastavartinā sahaikākinī vanacaraśaravarṣabhayapalāyitā vanam agāhiṣi | tatra ca me śārdūlanakhāvalīḍhanipatitāyāḥ pāṇibhraṣṭaḥ sa bālakaḥ kasya api kapilāśavasya kroḍam abhyalīyata | tacchavākarṣiṇaś ca vyāghrasya asūn iṣur iṣvasanayantramuktaḥ kṣaṇād alikṣat | bhilladārakaiḥ sa bālo 'pāhāri | sā tv ahaṃ mohasuptā kena api vṛṣṇipālenopanīya svaṃ kuṭīram āveśya kṛpayopakrāntavraṇā svasthībhūya svabhartur anti kam upatiṣṭhāsur asahāyatayā yāvad vyākulībhavāmi tāvan mamaiva duhitā saha yūnā kena api tam evoddeśam āgamat | sā bhṛśaṃ ruroda | ruditānte ca sā sārthaghāte svahastagatasya rājaputrasya kirātabhartṛhastagamanam ātmanaś ca kena api vanacareṇa vraṇaviropaṇam svasthāyāś ca punas tenopayantuṃ cintitā yā nikṛṣṭajātisamsargavaiklavyāt pratyākhyānapāruṣyam tad akṣameṇa ca amunā vivikte vipine svaśiraḥ kartanodyamam anena yūnā yadṛcchayā dṛṣṭena tasya durātmano hananam ātmanaś copayamanam ity akathayat | sa tu pṛṣṭo maithilendrasyaiva ko 'pi sevakaḥ kāraṇavilambī tanmārgānusārī jātaḥ | saha tena bhartur antikam upasṛtya putravṛttā ntena śrotram asya devyāḥ priyamvadāyāś ca adahāva |
children.translated_text: Here I am: once, while wandering about, I came to the land of the <s>Videhas</s>. Without entering <s>Mithilā</s> itself, I came to rest at some monastery outside [the city]. There, an elderly female ascetic offered me water for my feet, and I sat for a moment on the veranda floor. At the very sight of me, tears began flowing from her in an unbroken stream. 'What is this, mother? Tell me the reason,' I asked. She spoke sorrowfully: 'My dear child, surely you have heard that the lord of this <s>Mithilā</s> was named <s>Prahāravarman</s>. His closest friend was <s>Rājahaṃsa</s>, king of <s>Magadha</s>. Between their two beloved queens, <s>Vasumatī</s> and <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>, there was a matchless friendship, like that between [the divine pair] <s>Balaśambala</s>. Then <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>, wishing to see her dear friend <s>Vasumatī</s>, who was being celebrated for her first pregnancy, went to <s>Puṣpapura</s> together with her husband. And at that very time, a great battle arose between the <s>Mālava</s> [king] and the king of <s>Magadha</s>. In that battle, the king of <s>Magadha</s> met a fate that was hard to discern even in the slightest. The lord of <s>Maithila</s>, however, spared by the effort of the <s>Mālava</s> king, returned toward his own territory, but learning that the kingdom had been seized by the sons of his elder [brother] <s>Saṃhāravarman</s>—<s>Vikaṭavarman</s> and the others—he set out through a forest path, wishing to obtain military support from his nephew, the lord of <s>Suhma</s>, and was stripped of all his possessions by forest bandits. And I, alone with his younger son, an infant still in hand, fleeing in terror from the rain of arrows of forest-dwellers, plunged into the forest. There, as I fell, torn by the claws of a tiger, the child slipped from my hands and took shelter in the lap of some dead tawny horse. An arrow released from a mechanical bow instantly destroyed the life of the tiger that was dragging that carcass. The child was carried off by <s>Bhilla</s> boys. But I, fallen into a swoon, was brought by some cattle-herder of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan to his own hut, where he mercifully treated my wounds. Having recovered, while I was becoming distressed at being unable to go before my husband due to my helplessness, my own daughter arrived at that very place together with some young man. She wept bitterly. And at the end of her weeping, she told of how, in the massacre of the caravan, the prince in her own hand had fallen into the hands of a <s>Kirāta</s> husband [of another woman]; and how her own wounds had been healed by some forest-dweller; and how, once recovered, when she was intended by him for marriage, from her distress at contact with a man of low caste, she spoke harsh words of refusal; and how he, unable to bear this, attempted to cut off his own head in a secluded part of the forest; and how this young man, who happened to see him, killed that wicked one and took her [as his companion]. And that young man, when questioned, turned out to be some servant of the lord of <s>Maithila</s> himself, who had been delayed for a reason and had followed that path. Together with him, having approached her husband, we burned the ears of His Majesty and of <s>Priyaṃvadā</s> with the account of what had befallen the son.'

children.text: eṣo 'smi paryaṭann ekadā gato videheṣu | mithilām a-praviśya eva bahiḥ kva=cin maṭhi kāyā viśramitum etya kayā api vṛddha-tāpasyā datta-pādyaḥ kṣaṇam alinda-bhūmāv avāsthiṣi | tasyās tu mad-darśanād eva kim apy ābaddha-dhāram aśru prāvartata | ' kim etad amba kathaya kāraṇam ' iti pṛṣṭā sa-karuṇam ācaṣṭa - 'jaivātṛka nanu śrūyate patir asyā mithilāyāḥ prahāra-varmā nāmā asīt | tasya khalu magadha-rājo rāja-hamsaḥ paraṃ mitram āsīt | tayoś ca vallabhe bala-śambalayor iva vasumatī-priyamvade sakhyam a-pratimam adhattām | atha prathama-garbha-abhinanditāṃ tāṃ ca priya-sakhīṃ didṛkṣuḥ priyamvadā vasumatīṃ saha bhartrā puṣpa-puram agamat | tasminn eva ca samaye mālavena magadha-rājasya mahaj janyam ajani | tatra leśato 'pi dur-lakṣāṃ gatim agaman magadha-rājaḥ | maithila-indras tu mālava-indra-prayatna-prāṇitaḥ sva-viṣayaṃ prati nivṛtto jyeṣṭhasya samhāra-varmaṇaḥ sutair vikaṭa-varma-prabhṛtibhir vyāptaṃ rājyam ākarṇya svasrīyāt suhma-pater daṇḍa-avayavam āditsur aṭavī-patham avagāhya lubdhaka-lupta-sarva-svo 'bhūt | tat-sutena ca kanīyasā hasta-vartinā saha ekākinī vana-cara-śara-varṣa-bhaya-palāyitā vanam agāhiṣi | tatra ca me śārdūla-nakha-avalīḍha-nipatitāyāḥ pāṇi-bhraṣṭaḥ sa bālakaḥ kasya api kapilā-śavasya kroḍam abhyalīyata | tac-chava-ākarṣiṇaś ca vyāghrasya asūn iṣur iṣv-asana-yantra-muktaḥ kṣaṇād alikṣat | bhilla-dārakaiḥ sa bālo 'pāhāri | sā tv ahaṃ moha-suptā kena api vṛṣṇi-pālena upanīya svaṃ kuṭīram āveśya kṛpaya ūpakrānta-vraṇā svasthībhūya sva-bhartur anti kam upatiṣṭhāsur a-sahāyatayā yāvad vyākulībhavāmi tāvan mama eva duhitā saha yūnā kena api tam eva uddeśam āgamat | sā bhṛśaṃ ruroda | rudita-ante ca sā sārtha-ghāte sva-hasta-gatasya rāja-putrasya kirāta-bhartṛ-hasta-gamanam ātmanaś ca kena api vana-careṇa vraṇa-viropaṇam svasthāyāś ca punas tena upayantuṃ cintitā yā nikṛṣṭa-jāti-samsarga-vaiklavyāt pratyākhyāna-pāruṣyam tad a-kṣameṇa ca amunā vivikte vipine sva-śiraḥ kartana-udyamam anena yūnā yad-ṛcchayā dṛṣṭena tasya dur-ātmano hananam ātmanaś ca upayamanam ity akathayat | sa tu pṛṣṭo maithila-indrasya eva ko 'pi sevakaḥ kāraṇa-vilambī tan-mārga-anusārī jātaḥ | saha tena bhartur antikam upasṛtya putra-vṛttā ntena śrotram asya devyāḥ priyamvadāyāś ca adahāva |

sa ca rājā diṣṭadoṣāj jyeṣṭhaputraiś ciraṃ vigṛhya punar asahiṣṇutayā atimātraṃ ciraṃ prayudhya baddhaḥ | devī ca bandhanaṃ gamitā | dagdhā punar aham asminn api vārddhake hatajīvitam apārayantī hātuṃ pravrajyāṃ kila agrahīṣam | duhitā tu mama hatajīvitākṛṣṭā vikaṭavarmamahādevīṃ kalpasundarīṃ kila aśiśriyat | tau ced rājaputrau nirupadravāv eva avardhiṣyetām iyatā kālena tavemāṃ vayoavasthām asprakṣyetām | tayoś ca sator na dāyādā narendrasya prasahyakāriṇo bhaveyuḥ ' iti pramanyur abhiruroda | śrutvā ca tāpasīgiram aham api pravṛddhabāṣpo nigūḍham abhyadhām - 'yady evam amba samāśvasihi | nanv asti kaś cin munis tvayā tadavasthayā putrābhyupapādanārthaṃ yācitas tena sa labdho vardhitaś ca | vārteyam atimahatī | kim anayā | so 'ham asmi | śakyaś ca mayā asau vikaṭavarmā yathākathaṃcid upaśliṣya vyāpādayitum | anujāḥ punar atibahavaḥ tair api ghaṭante paurajānapadāḥ | māṃ tu na kaś=cid ihatya īdṛktayā jano jānāti | pitarāv api tāvan māṃ na samvidāte kim utetare | tad enam artham upāyena sādhayiṣyāmi ' ity agādiṣam | sā tu vṛddhā saruditaṃ pariṣvajya muhuḥ śirasy upāghrāya prasnutastanī sagadgadam agadat  'vatsa ciraṃ jīva | bhadraṃ tava | prasanno 'dya bhagavān vidhiḥ | adyaiva prahāravarmaṇy adhi videhā jātāḥ yataḥ pralambamānapīnabāhur bhavān apāram etac chokasāgaram adyottārayituṃ sthitaḥ | aho mahad bhāgadheyaṃ devyāḥ priyamvadāyāḥ ' iti harṣanirbharā snānabhojanādinā mām upācarat | aśiśriyaṃ ca asmin maṭhaikadeśe niśi kaṭaśayyām | acintayaṃ ca  'vinopadhinā ayam artho na sādhyaḥ | striyaś copadhīnām udbhavakṣetram | ato 'ntaḥpuravṛttāntam asyā avagamya taddvāreṇa kiñ=cij jālam ācareyam ' iti cintayaty eva mayi mahārṇavonmagnamārtaṇḍaturaṅgamaśvāsarayāvadhūteva vyāvartata triyāmā | samugragarbhavāsajaḍīkṛta iva mandapratāpo divasakaraḥ prādur āsīt |
children.translated_text: And that king, through an evil turn of fate, having long quarreled with his eldest sons and then, out of impatience, having fought against them for an exceedingly long time, was taken captive. The queen too was put into bondage. As for me—wretched and unable to abandon this hateful life even in such old age—I took, so they say, the vows of an ascetic. But my daughter, dragged on by her hateful life, took shelter, so they say, with <s>Kalpasundarī</s>, the chief queen of <s>Vikaṭavarman</s>. Had those two princes only grown up unharmed, by this much time they would have attained your present stage of life. And while those two lived, the kinsmen of the king could not have become tyrannical usurpers'—thus, overcome with grief, she wept aloud. And hearing the ascetic woman's words, I too, with welling tears, said in a veiled manner: 'If it is so, mother, take comfort. Surely there is some sage whom you, in that condition, entreated for the sake of obtaining the protection of a son, and by him that son was obtained and reared. This is news of the greatest importance. What need of more? I am that very one. And I am able, by some means or other, to draw near to that <s>Vikaṭavarman</s> and slay him. There are, moreover, very many younger kinsmen, and with them the townsfolk and country-folk are joined. But no one here knows me as such; even my own parents do not recognize me, how much less others. So by some stratagem I shall accomplish this object'—thus I spoke. And that old woman, embracing me with weeping, repeatedly kissing me upon the head, her breasts flowing [with maternal feeling], said in a faltering voice: 'My child, live long! Blessings upon you! Today the blessed Ordainer is gracious. This very day fortune has dawned upon <s>Prahāravarman</s>, since you—your full arms hanging down [in strength]—stand ready today to carry [us] across this shoreless ocean of grief. Ah, how great is the good fortune of Queen <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>!'—and, brimful of joy, she tended to me with bathing, food, and the rest. And I lay down that night upon a mat-bed in one part of that monastery. And I reflected: 'Without a stratagem this object cannot be accomplished. And women are the breeding-ground of stratagems. Therefore, having learned from her the events of the inner apartments, I shall through that means weave some net.' And even as I was thus reflecting, the three-watched night turned away, as though shaken off by the rush of the breath of the Sun's horses that surge up out of the great ocean. And the day-maker [the sun], his radiance faint, appeared as though dulled by his fierce dwelling in the womb [of the dawn].

children.text: sa ca rājā diṣṭa-doṣāj jyeṣṭha-putraiś ciraṃ vigṛhya punar a-sahiṣṇutayā atimātraṃ ciraṃ prayudhya baddhaḥ | devī ca bandhanaṃ gamitā | dagdhā punar aham asminn api vārddhake hata-jīvitam a-pārayantī hātuṃ pravrajyāṃ kila agrahīṣam | duhitā tu mama hata-jīvita-ākṛṣṭā vikaṭa-varma-mahā-devīṃ kalpa-sundarīṃ kila aśiśriyat | tau ced rāja-putrau nir-upadravāv eva avardhiṣyetām iyatā kālena tava imāṃ vayo-avasthām asprakṣyetām | tayoś ca sator na dāyādā nara-indrasya prasahya-kāriṇo bhaveyuḥ ' iti pra-manyur abhiruroda | śrutvā ca tāpasī-giram aham api pravṛddha-bāṣpo nigūḍham abhyadhām -- 'yady evam amba samāśvasihi | nanv asti kaś cin munis tvayā tad-avasthayā putra-abhyupapādana-arthaṃ yācitas tena sa labdho vardhitaś ca | vārta īyam atimahatī | kim anayā | so 'ham asmi | śakyaś ca mayā asau vikaṭa-varmā yathā-kathaṃ-cid upaśliṣya vyāpādayitum | anujāḥ punar atibahavaḥ tair api ghaṭante paura-jānapadāḥ | māṃ tu na kaś=cid ihatya īdṛktayā jano jānāti | pitarāv api tāvan māṃ na samvidāte kim uta itare | tad enam artham upāyena sādhayiṣyāmi ' ity agādiṣam | sā tu vṛddhā sa-ruditaṃ pariṣvajya muhuḥ śirasy upāghrāya prasnuta-stanī sa-gadgadam agadat - 'vatsa ciraṃ jīva | bhadraṃ tava | prasanno 'dya bhagavān vidhiḥ | adya eva prahāra-varmaṇy adhi videhā jātāḥ yataḥ pralambamāna-pīna-bāhur bhavān apāram etac choka-sāgaram adya uttārayituṃ sthitaḥ | aho mahad bhāgadheyaṃ devyāḥ priyamvadāyāḥ ' iti harṣa-nirbharā snāna-bhojana-ādinā mām upācarat | aśiśriyaṃ ca asmin maṭha-ekadeśe niśi kaṭa-śayyām | acintayaṃ ca - 'vina ūpadhinā ayam artho na sādhyaḥ | striyaś ca upadhīnām udbhava-kṣetram | ato 'ntaḥ-pura-vṛttāntam asyā avagamya tad-dvāreṇa kiñ=cij jālam ācareyam ' iti cintayaty eva mayi mahā-arṇava-unmagna-mārtaṇḍa-turaṅgama-śvāsa-raya-avadhūta īva vyāvartata tri-yāmā | samugra-garbha-vāsa-jaḍīkṛta iva manda-pratāpo divasa-karaḥ prādur āsīt |

utthāya avasāyitadinamukhaniyamavidhis tāṃ me mātaram avādiṣam - ' amba jālmasya vikaṭavarmaṇaḥ kac=cid antaḥpuravṛttāntam abhijānāsi ' ity anavasitavacanae eva mayi kā=cid aṅganā pratyadṛśyata | tāṃ ca avekṣya sā me dhātrī harṣāśrukuṇṭhitakaṇṭham ācaṣṭa - 'putri puṣkarike paśya bhartṛdārakam | ayam asāv akṛpayā mayā vane parityaktaḥ punar apy evam āgataḥ ' iti | sā tu harṣanirbharanipīḍitā ciraṃ prarudya bahu vilapya śāntā punaḥ svamātrā rājāntaḥpuravṛttāntākhyāne nyayujyata | uktaṃ ca tayā - 'kumāra kāmarūpeśvarasya kalindavarmanāmnaḥ kanyā kalpasundarī kalāsu rūpe ca apsaraso 'py atikrāntā patim abhibhūya vartate | tadekavallabhaḥ sa tu bahvavarodho 'pi vikaṭavarmā ' iti | tām avocam - ' upasarpaināṃ matprayuktair gandhamālyaiḥ | upajanaya ca asamānadoṣanindādinā svabhartari dveṣam | anurūpabha rtṛgāminīnāṃ ca vāsavadattādīnāṃ varṇanena grāhaya anuśayam | avarodhāntareṣu ca rājño vilasitāni su=gūḍhāny api prayatnena anviṣya prakāśayantī mānam asyā vardhaya ' iti | punar idam ambām avocam - ' ittham eva tvayā apy an=anyavyāpārayā nṛpāṅganā asāv upasthātavyā | pratyahaṃ ca yad yat tatra vṛttaṃ tad asmi tvayaiva bodhyaḥ | maduktā punar iyam udarkasvāduno 'smatkarmaṇaḥ prasādhanāya cchāyeva an=apāyinī kalpasundarīm anuvartatām ' iti | te ca tam arthaṃ tathaiva anvatiṣṭhatām | keṣucid dineṣu gateṣv ācaṣṭa māṃ madambā - 'vatsa mādhavīva picumandāśleṣiṇī yathā asau śocyam ātmānaṃ manyeta tathopapādya sthāpitā | kiṃ bhūyaḥ kṛtyam ' iti | punar aham abhilikhyātmanaḥ pratikṛtim ' iyam amuṣmai neyā | nītāṃ caināṃ nirvarṇya sā niyatam evaṃ vakṣyati - ' nanv asti kaś cid īdṛśākāraḥ pumān ' iti | pratibrūhy enām - ' yadi syāt tataḥ kim ' iti | tasya yad uttaraṃ sā dāsyati tad aham asmi pratibodhanīyaḥ ' iti | sā ' tathā ' iti rājakulam upasaṅkramya pratinivṛttā mām ekānte nyavedayat - 'vatsa darśito 'sau citrapaṭas tasyai mattakāśinyai | citrīyamāṇā ca asau ' bhuvanam idaṃ sanāthīkṛtaṃ yad deve 'pi kusumadhanvani nedṛśī vapuḥśrīḥ samnidhatte | citram etac citrataram | na ca tam avaimi ya īdṛśam ihatyo nirmimīte | kenedam ālikhitam ' ity ādṛtavatī vyāhṛtavatī ca | mayā ca smerayodīritam - ' devi sadṛśam ājñāpayasi | bhagavān makaraketur apy evaṃ sundara iti na śakyam eva sambhāvayitum | atha ca vistīrṇeyam arṇavanemiḥ | kvacid īdṛ śam api rūpaṃ daivaśaktyā sambhavet | atha tu yady evaṃrūpo rūpānurūpaśilpaśīlavidyājñānakauśalo yuvā mahākulīnaś ca kaś=cit samnihitaḥ syāt sa kiṃ lapsyate ' iti | tayoktam - ' amba kiṃ bravīmi | śarīraṃ dṛdayaṃ jīvitam iti sarvam idam alpam anarhaṃ ca | tato na kiñ=cil lapsyate | na ced ayaṃ vipralambhas tasya amuṣya darśanānubhavena yathedaṃ cakṣuś caritārthaṃ bhavet tathā anugrahaḥ kāryaḥ ' iti | bhūyo 'pi mayā dṛḍhatarīkartum upanyastam  ' asti ko 'pi rājasūnur nigūḍhaṃ caran | amuṣya vasantotsave saha sakhībhir nagaropavanavihāriṇī ratir iva vigrahiṇī yadṛcchayā darśanapathaṃ gatā asi | gataś ca asau kāmaśaraikalakṣya tāṃ mām anvavartiṣṭa | mayā ca vām anyoanyānurūpair durlabhair ākārādibhir guṇātiśayaiś ca preryamāṇayā tadracitair eva kusumaśekharasraganulepanādibhiś ciram upāsitā asi | sādṛśyaṃ ca svam anena svayam eva abhilikhya tvatsamādhigāḍhatvadarśanāya preṣi tam | eṣa ced artho children.translated_text: Having risen and completed the morning observances and ritual duties, I addressed that mother of mine: 'Mother, do you perchance know the inner affairs of the palace of the wretched <s>Vikaṭavarman</s>?' Even as I had not finished speaking, a certain woman came into view. Upon seeing her, my nurse, her throat choked with tears of joy, said: 'Daughter <s>Puṣkarikā</s>, look — the young master! He is the very one whom I cruelly abandoned in the forest, and yet he has come back again.' She, however, overwhelmed by the fullness of her joy, having wept long and lamented greatly, grew calm and was then engaged by her own mother in narrating the affairs of the royal inner palace. And she said: '<s>Kumāra</s>, the daughter of the lord of <s>Kāmarūpa</s>, named <s>Kalindavarman</s>, is <s>Kalpasundarī</s> — she who has surpassed even the <s>Apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs) in arts and beauty, and she dominates her husband. Yet that <s>Vikaṭavarman</s>, though he has many women in his harem, is devoted to her alone.' I said to her: 'Approach her with perfumes and garlands sent by me. And engender in her hatred toward her own husband by censuring him for faults unmatched by others. And by describing women like <s>Vāsavadattā</s> and others who went to husbands worthy of them, instill in her regret. And by diligently seeking out and revealing the king's dalliances with other harem women, even those most deeply concealed, increase her pride.' Again I addressed my mother: 'In just this manner, you too, with no other occupation, must attend upon that queen. And each day, whatever transpires there, I must be informed of it by you yourself. Furthermore, let this woman, instructed by me, follow <s>Kalpasundarī</s> like a shadow that never departs, for the accomplishment of our enterprise whose fruit will be sweet in the end.' And those two carried out that plan exactly so. After some days had passed, my mother reported to me: 'My child, like a <s>mādhavī</s> creeper clinging to a neem tree, she has been brought to the point where she considers herself pitiable, and there she has been established. What more is to be done?' Then I, having drawn a portrait of myself, said: 'This is to be taken to her. And upon examining it once it is brought, she will surely say: "Is there indeed some man of such appearance?" Reply to her: "If there were, then what?" Whatever answer she gives to that, I must be informed of it.' She, saying 'So be it,' went to the royal palace and upon returning reported to me in private: 'My child, that painted canvas was shown to that intoxicated-eyed woman. And she, gazing at it with wonder, said reverently: "The world is made blessed, for even in the god <s>Kusumadhanvan</s> (the flower-armed Kāma) such bodily splendor does not reside. This picture is more wondrous than any wonder. And I do not know who it is that creates such a likeness here. By whom was this painted?" And I said with a smile: "<s>Devī</s>, you speak fittingly. It is indeed impossible to suppose that even the blessed <s>Makaraketu</s> (the fish-bannered Kāma) is so beautiful. And yet this ocean-girdled earth is vast. Somewhere, by the power of fate, such a form might exist. But if a youth of such form, endowed with skills, character, learning, knowledge, and dexterity befitting his beauty, and of great lineage, were present — what would he obtain?" She replied: "Mother, what can I say? Body, heart, life — all this is too little and unworthy. From that he would obtain nothing. If this is not a deception, then by the experience of beholding him, so that these eyes may be fulfilled in their purpose, that favor should be granted." I pressed further to make her resolve firmer: "There is a certain prince who moves about in disguise. During the spring festival, as you were strolling in the city garden with your companions, like <s>Rati</s> (Love's consort) incarnate, you chanced to come within his sight. And he, become the sole target of <s>Kāma's</s> arrows, followed me on your account. And I, impelled by the rare and matchless qualities of form and character in you both, so perfectly suited to each other, have long attended upon you with flower-chaplets, garlands, unguents, and the like, all prepared by him. And having himself drawn his own likeness, he has sent it to demonstrate the depth of his devotion to you. If this matter is settled, then for him — who possesses surpassing valor, courage, wisdom, and prowess beyond the human measure — nothing whatsoever is difficult. I could show him to you this very day. A rendezvous should be arranged." She, having reflected for a moment, then said: "Mother, this is no longer to be concealed from you at this point. Therefore I shall tell you. My father and King <s>Prahāravarman</s> had a great friendship between them. And my mother <s>Mānavatī's</s> dear companion was Queen <s>Priyamvadā</s>. By those two, even before they had offspring, an agreement was made: 'Whichever of us has a son, to him the daughter of whichever has a daughter shall be given.' But my father, when I was born and <s>Priyamvadā</s> had lost her child, gave me by fate's decree to <s>Vikaṭavarman</s> who had been requesting me. And this man is cruel, a betrayer of his father, not of very pleasing appearance, unskilled in the arts of love, with little interest in arts, poetry, drama, and the like, mad with the arrogance of valor, a vile boaster, a liar, and one who bestows favors in the wrong place. This husband does not greatly please me, especially in these days. For in the garden, disregarding even <s>Puṣkarikā</s>, who is as dear to me as my own heart, though she stood nearby, he gratified one named <s>Ramayantikā</s>, who is ignorant of her own worth and has bound herself in jealous rivalry with me — a woman no different from a slave — and he adorned her with flowers he himself had plucked from the <s>campaka</s> creeper that I had reared as my own child. On the jeweled couch within the painted pavilion that I had used and then relinquished, he sported with her. And an unworthy man who has also begun to show contempt — why should one wait any longer? And the fear of the next world is eclipsed by suffering in this one. For unbearable indeed to women, who are creatures whose hearts are pierced by the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless god of love), is the torment of being yoked to the company of an unloved person. Therefore, bring me together with that man today, in the <s>mādhavī</s> bower in the garden. For merely by hearing tidings of him, my mind has become excessively attached. And here is this heap of wealth. With this, having established him in his rightful position, I shall serve him alone and thus live out my life." I too assented to all this and returned. Henceforth, the young master is the authority.' Then, having learned from her very account the layout of the inner palace, the stations of the interior guards, and the grounds of the pleasure garden in all their divisions, when the sun's orb was reddening like the peak of the setting mountain streaming with blood, when darkness had spread, filling the sky like a mass of smoke from the embers of the sun-bird quenched by the waters of the western ocean, when the moon — patron of the embrace of others' wives, as if risen to serve as my preceptor, boasting of the seizure of the <s>Guru's</s> (Jupiter's) wife, foremost among the planets — had its splendor kindled by the moon-disk that appeared like the lotus-face of <s>Kalpasundarī</s> herself, smiling with the first flush of passionate eagerness for my sight, and when the god <s>Kusumadhanvan</s> (Kāma), his might ablaze, was setting forth to conquer the world, I took to my appointed bed. And I reflected: 'This enterprise is all but accomplished. Yet from transgressing with another's wife, there would be injury to <s>dharma</s>. But even that, the authors of the <s>śāstras</s> have sanctioned when two of the three aims — <s>artha</s> (wealth) and <s>kāma</s> (desire) — are obtained. And this transgression has been committed by me as part of a plan for liberating my elders from bondage; and even that sin, once expiated by however small a portion of <s>dharma</s>, would leave me whole.' But then, 'Upon hearing of this, what will lord <s>Rājavāhana</s> or my friends say?' — absorbed in such anxious thought, I was seized by sleep. And in a dream the blessed elephant-faced god (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) appeared. And he said: 'Good <s>Upahāravarman</s>, let there be no misgiving in you, for you are a portion of myself. That woman of excellent complexion is the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), accustomed to being cherished amidst the mass of <s>Śaṅkara's</s> (Śiva's) matted locks. And she once, unable to bear being churned by me, cursed me: "Go, become a mortal!" And she was cursed by me in turn: "Just as here you are enjoyed by many, so too, having attained human birth, become one shared by many." And she entreated me: "Having been wife to one man first, may I then attend upon you alone and delight for as long as I live." Therefore this matter is destined to be — you should have no apprehension about it.' And having awakened, filled with joy, I passed that day too in remembering the anticipation of the appointed tryst with my beloved and related matters. The next day, <s>Anaṅga</s> (Kāma), whose course is never otherwise, rained his shower of arrows upon me alone. And the luminous lake of the sun dried up. And a mire of darkness spread forth. Clad in dark garments, my girdle tightly fastened, sword in hand, carrying the requisite implements, and remembering the tokens of recognition given by my mother, I approached the moat around the royal palace, which was full of water. Then, at the entrance to my mother's house, taking a bamboo pole that <s>Puṣkarikā</s> had placed there beforehand, and with her having put it down across the moat, I vaulted over the rampart wall. Having climbed up, I descended to the ground by a stairway leading down from the upper terrace of the gateway, which was constructed of baked bricks. Having descended and passing through an avenue of <s>vakula</s> trees, proceeding a little along a path bordered by <s>campaka</s> rows, I heard to the north the plaintive cry of a pair of <s>cakravāka</s> birds. Then, going northward along a path of <s>pāṭalī</s> trees, through the interior of a broad palace wall reachable by touch, traversing about a bowshot's distance, then turning east along a sandy path adorned on both sides with clusters of <s>piṇḍī</s> and <s>bhāṇḍīra</s> trees, proceeding a little to the north, I then entered a southward avenue of mango trees. And there, in a deeper recess, I discerned by the light of a lamp-wick faintly gleaming as if from a slightly opened casket, a bower of <s>mādhavī</s> creepers with a jeweled platform constructed within its interior. Entering, on one side, I opened the door to the inner chamber — a door surrounded by rows of <s>kuraṇṭaka</s> shrubs in full bloom forming an unbroken wall, a door overspread with trailing crimson <s>aśoka</s> creepers that had fallen to the ground, spotted with the marks of fresh flower-buds, and reddened with layers of new shoots — and I stepped inside. There was a well-spread couch of flowers, and lotus-leaf receptacles containing the accessories for lovemaking, a fan of ivory, and a pitcher filled with fragrant water. Having sat down and rested a moment, I inhaled a surpassing fragrance. And I heard a soft, soft sound of footsteps. The very instant I heard it, I came out of the trysting-chamber and stood with my body concealed beside the trunk of a crimson <s>aśoka</s> tree. And she, the beautiful-browed one, desiring no meager love, approached slowly, and not seeing me there, was greatly distressed. And like an intoxicated royal goose, she uttered words lovely with the sweet stammering of passion in her throat: 'Clearly I have been deceived. There is no means to go on living. O heart, why do you impose this impossible thing as though it were possible, and why do you languish so for what cannot be? O blessed <s>Pañcabāṇaka</s> (five-arrowed Kāma), what offense have I committed against you, that you burn me thus and yet do not reduce me to ashes?' Then I, revealing myself, holding forth the uncovered lamp, said: 'O proud beauty, surely you have greatly wronged the mind-born god (<s>Kāma</s>), for <s>Rati</s> (Love's consort), who is the very life of that god, has been put to shame by your form: the bow-staff by your brow-creepers, the bowstring of bee-garlands by the luster of your dark tresses, the weapons by the glances raining from the corners of your eyes, the great saffron-colored banner-cloth by the rays of your lip-petals, his first ally the Malaya breeze by the breath of your sighs more potent in fragrance, the cuckoo's song by your exceedingly sweet murmurings, the flower-banner by your arm-stalks, the pair of full ceremonial vessels marking the commencement of his world-conquest by the pair of pitcher-like breasts upon your bosom, the pleasure-lake by the circle of your navel, the war-chariot by the circle of your hips, the pair of pillars of the jeweled gateway of Love's abode by the pair of your thighs, and the sport-earring's tender shoot by the radiance of the soles of your feet. Therefore <s>Mīnaketu</s> (the fish-bannered Kāma) torments you in his very own domain. But me, who am without offense, he afflicts even more — and therein lies his fault. So be gracious, O beautiful one; revive me, bitten by the serpent of <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless Kāma), with the life-giving herbs of your sidelong glances.' And I embraced her. And I made love to that woman of wide eyes lovely without cosmetic adornment. And perceiving her, her purpose fulfilled, with eyes moving languidly in the afterglow, the roots of her cheeks broken by faintly emerging lines of perspiration, prattling ceaselessly in sweet murmurs, marked by the exchange of impressions from reddened teeth and fingernails, her limbs exceedingly relaxed, as if in a swoon — loosening my own mental and bodily composure, I brought myself too into the same state as hers. Released from our union at that instant, experiencing the rites that conclude lovemaking, we rested a moment as though long familiar with each other, in exceedingly intimate trust. Then I, sighing hotly and deeply, with a somewhat sorrowful gaze, embraced her with arms stretched out tremblingly, not too tightly, and kissed her not too distinctly. And she, her face wet with tears, said: 'If you depart, my lord, consider that this life of mine departs with you. Take me too. If not, then this servant is of no use.' And she brought her joined palms to her forehead. And I addressed her: 'O innocent one, what man possessed of sense would not rejoice in a woman who desires him? If your resolve to favor me is firm, then carry out what I instruct without hesitation. Show the king in private the portrait bearing my likeness. And say: "Has this form reached the utmost limit of manly beauty, or has it not?" "Indeed it has" — so he will surely reply. Then say further: "If so, there is a certain ascetic woman, emboldened by her wanderings in foreign lands, who is like a mother to me. She, presenting this painted likeness, told me: 'There exists such a <s>mantra</s> by which you, having fasted on the sacred day, in a secluded place, after the priests have offered oblations and the seven-tongued fire has been consecrated, alone at night, having offered a hundred <s>candana</s> (sandalwood) fire-sticks, handfuls of <s>karpūra</s> (camphor), and abundant silk garments into the fire, shall become of such form. And then you shall ring a bell. And your husband, summoned by the ringing of the bell, having told you every secret with closed eyes, if he embraces you, this form shall pass over to him. And you shall become just as you were before in appearance. If this pleases you and your beloved, then there must be no breach of faith in this rite.' If this body is what you desire, then having deliberated together with his trusted ministers, younger brothers, and the people of city and countryside, and with their approval too, he must stand ready to undertake the rite." He will surely consent. Then, at this very crossroads of the pleasure-garden, I, having performed an <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> (Atharva Vedic) rite with a slaughtered sacrificial animal and made offerings, when the golden-seeded fire has been consecrated, having entered under cover of its smoke and soot, shall station myself in this very creeper-bower. And you, in the deep hours of early evening, whispering in <s>Vikaṭavarman's</s> ear with a playful smile, shall say: "You are a rogue and ungrateful. With the beauty obtained through my grace, a beauty that would be a festival for the eyes of the world, you will go and delight my co-wives. I would not perform the raising of a <s>vetāla</s> (vampire spirit) only for my own destruction." When he has heard these words of yours, whatever he says, you shall come to me alone and report it. From that point on, I myself shall know what to do. And have <s>Puṣkarikā</s> sweep away my footprints in the garden.' She, saying 'So be it,' revering my words as though they were the teaching of a <s>śāstra</s>, her passion for love still unsated, somehow, with great reluctance, went back to the inner palace. And I too, going out the same way I had entered, returned to my own dwelling.

children.text: utthāya avasāyita-dina-mukha-niyama-vidhis tāṃ me mātaram avādiṣam -- ' amba jālmasya vikaṭa-varmaṇaḥ kac=cid antaḥ-pura-vṛttāntam abhijānāsi ' ity an-avasita-vacanae eva mayi kā=cid aṅganā pratyadṛśyata | tāṃ ca avekṣya sā me dhātrī harṣa-aśru-kuṇṭhita-kaṇṭham ācaṣṭa -- 'putri puṣkarike paśya bhartṛ-dārakam | ayam asāv a-kṛpayā mayā vane parityaktaḥ punar apy evam āgataḥ ' iti | sā tu harṣa-nirbhara-nipīḍitā ciraṃ prarudya bahu vilapya śāntā punaḥ sva-mātrā rāja-antaḥ-pura-vṛttānta-ākhyāne nyayujyata | uktaṃ ca tayā -- 'kumāra kāma-rūpa-īśvarasya kalinda-varma-nāmnaḥ kanyā kalpa-sundarī kalāsu rūpe ca apsaraso 'py atikrāntā patim abhibhūya vartate | tad-eka-vallabhaḥ sa tu bahv-avarodho 'pi vikaṭa-varmā ' iti | tām avocam -- ' upasarpa enāṃ mat-prayuktair gandha-mālyaiḥ | upajanaya ca a-samāna-doṣa-nindā-ādinā sva-bhartari dveṣam | anurūpa-bha rtṛ-gāminīnāṃ ca vāsava-dattā-ādīnāṃ varṇanena grāhaya anuśayam | avarodha-antareṣu ca rājño vilasitāni su=gūḍhāny api prayatnena anviṣya prakāśayantī mānam asyā vardhaya ' iti | punar idam ambām avocam -- ' ittham eva tvayā apy an=anya-vyāpārayā nṛpa-aṅganā asāv upasthātavyā | praty-ahaṃ ca yad yat tatra vṛttaṃ tad asmi tvaya aiva bodhyaḥ | mad-uktā punar iyam udarka-svāduno 'smat-karmaṇaḥ prasādhanāya cchāya īva an=apāyinī kalpa-sundarīm anuvartatām ' iti | te ca tam arthaṃ tatha aiva anvatiṣṭhatām | keṣu-cid dineṣu gateṣv ācaṣṭa māṃ mad-ambā -- 'vatsa mādhavi īva picumanda-āśleṣiṇī yathā asau śocyam ātmānaṃ manyeta tatha ūpapādya sthāpitā | kiṃ bhūyaḥ kṛtyam ' iti | punar aham abhilikhyā atmanaḥ pratikṛtim ' iyam amuṣmai neyā | nītāṃ ca enāṃ nirvarṇya sā niyatam evaṃ vakṣyati -- ' nanv asti kaś cid īdṛśa-ākāraḥ pumān ' iti | pratibrūhy enām -- ' yadi syāt tataḥ kim ' iti | tasya yad uttaraṃ sā dāsyati tad aham asmi pratibodhanīyaḥ ' iti | sā ' tathā ' iti rāja-kulam upasaṅkramya pratinivṛttā mām ekānte nyavedayat -- 'vatsa darśito 'sau citra-paṭas tasyai matta-kāśinyai | citrīyamāṇā ca asau ' bhuvanam idaṃ sa-nāthīkṛtaṃ yad deve 'pi kusuma-dhanvani nā idṛśī vapuḥ-śrīḥ samnidhatte | citram etac citrataram | na ca tam avaimi ya īdṛśam ihatyo nirmimīte | kena idam ālikhitam ' ity ādṛtavatī vyāhṛtavatī ca | mayā ca smeraya ūdīritam -- ' devi sadṛśam ājñāpayasi | bhagavān makara-ketur apy evaṃ sundara iti na śakyam eva sambhāvayitum | atha ca vistīrṇa īyam arṇava-nemiḥ | kvacid īdṛ śam api rūpaṃ daiva-śaktyā sambhavet | atha tu yady evaṃ-rūpo rūpa-anurūpa-śilpa-śīla-vidyā-jñāna-kauśalo yuvā mahā-kulīnaś ca kaś=cit samnihitaḥ syāt sa kiṃ lapsyate ' iti | taya ūktam -- ' amba kiṃ bravīmi | śarīraṃ dṛdayaṃ jīvitam iti sarvam idam alpam an-arhaṃ ca | tato na kiñ=cil lapsyate | na ced ayaṃ vipralambhas tasya amuṣya darśana-anubhavena yatha īdaṃ cakṣuś carita-arthaṃ bhavet tathā anugrahaḥ kāryaḥ ' iti | bhūyo 'pi mayā dṛḍhatarīkartum upanyastam - ' asti ko 'pi rāja-sūnur nigūḍhaṃ caran | amuṣya vasanta-utsave saha sakhībhir nagara-upavana-vihāriṇī ratir iva vigrahiṇī yad-ṛcchayā darśana-pathaṃ gatā asi | gataś ca asau kāma-śara-eka-lakṣya tāṃ mām anvavartiṣṭa | mayā ca vām anyo-anya-anurūpair dur-labhair ākāra-ādibhir guṇa-atiśayaiś ca preryamāṇayā tad-racitair eva kusuma-śekhara-srag-anulepana-ādibhiś ciram upāsitā asi | sādṛśyaṃ ca svam anena svayam eva abhilikhya tvat-samādhi-gāḍhatva-darśanāya preṣi tam | eṣa ced artho niścitas tasya amuṣya atimānuṣa-prāṇa-sattva-prajñā-prakarṣasya na kiñ=cid duṣkaraṃ nāma | tam adya eva darśayeyam | saṅketo deyaḥ ' iti | tayā tu kiñ=cid iva dhyātvā punar abhihitam - ' amba tava na etad idānīṃ gopya-tamam | ataḥ kathayāmi | mama tātasya rājñā prahāra-varmaṇā saha mahatī prītir āsīt | mātuś ca me mānavatyāḥ priya-vayasyā devī priyamvadā āsīt | tābhyāṃ punar a-jāta-apatyābhyām eva kṛtaḥ samayo abhūt -- ' āvayoḥ putravatyāḥ putrāya duhitṛmatyā duhitā deyā ' iti | tātas tu māṃ jātāṃ pranaṣṭa-apatyā priyamvada īti prārthayamānāya vikaṭa-varmaṇe daivād dattavān | ayaṃ ca niṣṭhuraḥ pitṛ-drohī na atyupasanna-saṃsthānaḥ kāma-upacāreṣv a-labdha-vaicakṣaṇyaḥ kalāsu kāvya-nāṭaka-ādiṣu manda-abhiniveśaḥ śaurya-unmādī dur-vikatthano an-ṛta-vādī ca a-sthāna-varṣī | na atirocate me eṣa bhartā viśeṣataś ca eṣu vāsareṣu | yad ayam udyāne mad-antaraṅga-bhūtāṃ puṣkarikām apy upānta-vartinīm an-ādṛtya mayi baddha-sāpatnya-matsarām an-ātma-jñām ātma-nāṭakīyāṃ ramayantikā nāma apatya-nir=viśeṣaṃ mat-samvardhitāyāś campaka-latāyāḥ svayam avacitābhiḥ su=manobhir alam akārṣīt | mad-upabhukta-mukte citra-kūṭa-garbha-vedikā-gate ratna-talpe tayā saha vyahārṣīt | a-yogyaś ca pumān avajñātuṃ ca pravṛttaḥ | tat kim ity apekṣyate | para-loka-bhayaṃ ca aihikena duḥkhena antaritam | a=viṣahyaṃ hi yoṣitām an=aṅga-śara-niṣaṅgī bhūta-cetasām an=iṣṭa-jana-samvāsa-yantraṇā-duḥkham | ato 'munā puruṣeṇa mām adya udyāna-mādhavī-gṛhe samāgamaya | tad-vārtā-śravaṇa-mātreṇa eva hi mama atimātraṃ mano 'nuraktam | asti ca ayam artha-rāśiḥ | anena amuṣya pade pratiṣṭhāpya tam eva atyantam upacarya jīviṣyāmi ' iti | mayā api tad abhyupetya pratyāgatam | ataḥ paraṃ bhartṛ-dārakaḥ pramāṇam ' iti | tatas tasyā eva sakāśād antaḥ-pura-niveśam antar-vamśika-puruṣa-sthānāni pramada-vana-pradeśān api vibhāgena avagamya asta-giri-kūṭa-pāta-kṣubhita-śoṇita iva śoṇībhavati bhānu-bimbe paścima-ambudhi-payaḥ-pāta-nirvāpita-pataṅga-aṅgāra-dhūma-sambhāra iva bharita-nabhasi tamasi vijṛmbhite para-dāra-parāmarśa-unmukhasya mamā acāryakam iva kartum utthite guru-parigraha-ślāghini graha-agre-sare kṣapā-kare kalpa-sundarī-vadana-puṇḍarīkeṇa iva mad-darśana-atirāga-prathama-upanatena smayamānena candra-maṇḍalena sandhukṣamāṇa-tejasi bhuvana-vijigīṣā-udyate deve kusuma-dhanvani yathā-ucitaṃ śayanīyam abhaje | vyacītaraṃ ca - ' siddha-prāya eva ayam arthaḥ | kiṃ tu para-kalatra-laṅghanād dharma-pīḍā bhavet | sā apy artha-kāmayor dvayor upalambhe śāstra-kārair anumata aiva iti | guru-jana-bandha-mokṣa-upāya-sandhinā mayā ca eṣa vyatikramaḥ kṛtas tad api pāpaṃ nirhṛtya kiyatyā api dharma-kalayā māṃ samagrayed iti | api tv etad ākarṇya devo rāja-vāhanaḥ su-hṛdo vā kiṃ nu vakṣyanti ' iti cintā-para-adhīna eva nidrayā parāmṛśye | adṛśyata ca svapne hasti-vaktro bhagavān | āha sma ca - ' saumya upahāra-varman mā sma te dur-vikalpo bhūt | yatas tvam asi mad-amśaḥ | śaṅkara-jaṭā-bhāra-lālana-ucitā sura-sarid asau vara-varṇinī | sā ca kadā=cin mad-viloḍana-a=sahiṣṇur mām aśapat - - ' ehi martyatvam ' iti | aśapyata mayā ca - ' yatha īha bahu-bhogyā tathā prāpya api mānuṣyakam an=eka-sādhāraṇī bhava ' iti | abhyarthitaś ca anayā ' eka-pūrvāṃ punas tvām eva upacarya yāvaj-jīvaṃ rameyam ' iti | tad ayam artho bhavya eva bhavatā nir=āśaṅkyaḥ ' iti | pratibudhya ca prīti-yuktas tad-ahar api priyā-saṅketa-vyatikara-ādi-smaraṇena aham anaiṣam | anye-dyur an-anyathā-vṛttir an-aṅgo mayy eva iṣu-varṣam avarṣat | aśuṣyac ca jyotiṣmataḥ prabhā-mayaṃ saraḥ | prāsarac ca timira-mayaḥ kardamaḥ | kārdamika-nivasanaś ca dṛḍhatara-parikaraḥ khaḍga-pāṇir upahṛta-upaskaraḥ smaran mātṛ-dattāny abhijñānāni rāja-mandira-parikhām ud-ambhasam upātiṣṭham | atha upa khātaṃ mātṛ-gṛha-dvāre puṣkarikayā prathama-samnidhāpitāṃ veṇu-yaṣṭim ādāya tayā śāyitayā ca parikhāṃ sthāpitayā ca prākāra-bhittim alaṅghayam | adhiruhya pakva-iṣṭaka-citena gopura-upari-tala-adhirohiṇā sopāna-pathena bhuvam avātaram | avatīrṇaś ca vakula-vīthīm atikramya campaka-āvali-vartmanā manāg iva upasṛtya uttarāhi karuṇaṃ cakra-vāka-mithuna-ravam aśṛṇavam | punar udīcā pāṭali-pathena sparśa-labhya-viśāla-saudha-kuḍya-udareṇa śara-kṣepam iva gatvā punaḥ prācā piṇḍī-bhāṇḍīra-khaṇḍa-maṇḍita-ubhaya-pārśvena saikata-pathena kiñ=cid uttaram atikramya punar avācīṃ cūta-vīthīm agāhiṣi | tataś ca gahanataram udara-uparacita-ratna-vedikaṃ mādhavī-latā-maṇḍapam īṣad-vivṛta-samudgaka-unmiṣita-bhāsā dīpa-vartyā nyarūpayam | praviśya ca eka-pā rśve phulla-puṣpa-nirantara-kuraṇṭa-pota-paṅkti-bhitti-parigataṃ garbha-gṛham avani-patita-aruṇa-aśoka-latā-mayam abhinava-kusuma-koraka-pulaka-lāñchitaṃ pratyagra-pravāla-paṭala-pāṭalaṃ kapāṭam udghāṭya prāvikṣam | tatra cā asīt sv-āstīrṇaṃ kusuma-śayanam surata-upakaraṇa-vastu-garbhāś ca kamalinī-palāśa-sampuṭāḥ danta-mayas tāla-vṛntaḥ surabhi-salila-bharitaś ca bhṛṅgārakaḥ | samupaviśya muhūrtaṃ viśrāntaḥ parimalam atiśayavantam āghrāsiṣam | aśrauṣaṃ ca manda-mandaṃ pada-śabdam | śrutva aiva saṅketa-gṛhān nirgatya rakta-aśoka-skandha-pārśva-vyavahita-aṅga-yaṣṭiḥ sthito 'smi | sā ca su-bhrūr a=suṣīma-kāmā śanair upetya tatra mām a-dṛṣṭvā balavad avyathiṣṭa | vyasṛjac ca matta-rāja-hamsi īva kaṇṭha-rāga-valgu-gadgadāṃ giram -- ' vyaktam asmi vipralabdhā | na asty upāyaḥ prāṇitum | ayi hṛdaya kim idam a=kāryaṃ kāryavad adhyasya tad-a=sambhavena kim evam uttāmyasi | bhagavan pañca-bāṇakas tava aparādhaḥ kṛto mayā yad evaṃ dahasi na ca bhasmīkaroṣi ' iti | atha aham āvirbhūya vivṛta-dīpa-bhājanaḥ ' bhāmini nanu bahv aparāddhaṃ bhavatyā citta-janmano yad amuṣya jīvita-bhūtā ratir ākṛtyā kadarthitā dhanur-yaṣṭir bhrū-latābhyām bhramara-mālā-mayī jyā nīla-alaka-dyutibhiḥ astrāṇy apāṅga-vīkṣita-vṛṣṭibhiḥ mahā-rajana-dhvaja-paṭa-amśukaṃ danta-cchada-mayūkha-jālaiḥ prathama-suhṛn malaya-mārutaḥ parimala-paṭīyasā niḥśvāsa-pavanena parabhṛta-rutam ati-mañjulaiḥ pralāpaiḥ puṣpa-mayī patākā bhuja-yaṣṭibhyām dig-vijaya-ārambha-pūrṇa-kumbha-mithunam uroja-kumbha-yugalena krīḍā-saro nābhi-maṇḍalena samnāhya-rathaḥ śroṇi-maṇḍalena bhava-ratna-toraṇa-sta mbha-yugalam ūru-yugalena līlā-karṇa-kisalayaṃ caraṇa-tala-prabhābhiḥ | ataḥ sthānae eva tvāṃ dunoti mīna-ketuḥ | māṃ punar an=aparādham adhikam āyāsayati ity eṣa eva tasya doṣaḥ | tat prasīda sundari jīvaya māṃ jīvana-auṣadhibhir iva apāṅgair an=aṅga-bhujaṅga-daṣṭam | ' ity āśliṣṭavān | arīramaṃ ca an=aṅga-rāga-peśala-viśāla-locanām | avasita-arthāṃ cā arakta-valita-īkṣaṇām īṣat-sveda-rekhā-udbheda-jarjarita-kapola-mūlām an=argala-kala-pralāpinīm aruṇa-daśana-kara-ruha-arpaṇa-vyatikarām atyartha-pariślatha-aṅgīm ārtām iva lakṣayitvā mānasīṃ śārīrīṃ ca dhāraṇāṃ śithilayann ātmānam api tayā samāna-artham āpādayam | tat-kṣaṇa-vimukta-saṅgatau rata-avasānikaṃ vidhim anubhavantau cira-paricitāv iva atigūḍha-viśrambhau kṣaṇam avātiṣṭhāvahi | punar aham uṣṇam āyataṃ ca niḥśvasya kiñ=cid-dīna-dṛṣṭiḥ sa-cakita-prasāritābhyāṃ bhujābhyām enām an=atipīḍaṃ pariṣvajya na ativiśadam acumbiṣam | aśru-mukhī tu sā ' yadi prayāsi nātha prayātam eṣa me jīvitaṃ gaṇaya | naya mām api | na ced asau dāsa-jano niṣ-prayojanaḥ | ' ity añjalim avatamsatām anaiṣīt | avādiṣaṃ ca tām -- ' ayi mugdhe kaḥ sa-cetanaḥ striyam abhikāmayamānāṃ na abhinandati | yadi mad-anugraha-niścalas tava abhisandhir ācara a=vicāraṃ mad-upadiṣṭam | ādarśaya rahasi rājñe mat-sādṛśya-garbhaṃ citra-paṭam | ācakṣva ca - ' kim iyam ākṛ tiḥ puruṣa-saundaryasya pāram ārūḍhā na vā ' iti | ' bāḍham ārūḍhā ' iti nūnam asau vakṣyati | brūhi bhūyaḥ -- ' yady evam asti kā api tāpasī deśa-antara-bhramaṇa-labdha-prāgalbhyā mama ca mātṛ-bhūtā | taya īdam ālekhya-rūpaṃ puraskṛtya aham uktā -- ' so 'sti tādṛśo mantro yena tvam upoṣitā parvaṇi viviktāyāṃ bhūmau puro-hitair huta-mukte sapta-arciṣi naktam ekākinī śataṃ candana-samidhaḥ karpūra-muṣṭīḥ paṭṭa-vastrāṇi ca prabhūtāni hutvā bhaviṣyasy evam-ākṛtiḥ | atha cālayiṣyasi ghaṇṭām | ghaṇṭā-puṭa-kvaṇita-āhūtaś ca bhartā bhavatyai sarva-rahasyam ākhyāya nimīlita-akṣo yadi tvām āliṅget iyam ākṛ tir amum upasaṅkrāmet | tvaṃ tu bhaviṣyasi yathā purā-ākāra aiva | yadi bhavatyai bhavat-priyāya ca evaṃ roceta na ca asmin vidhau visamvādaḥ kāryaḥ ' iti | vapuś ced idaṃ tava abhimataṃ saha suhṛn-mantribhir anujaiḥ paura-jānapadaiś ca saṃpradhārya teṣām apy anumate karmaṇy abhimukhena stheyam ' iti | sa niyatam abhyupaiṣyati | punar asyām eva pramada-vana-vāṭī-śṛṅgāṭikāyām ātharvaṇikena vidhinā sañjñapita-paśunā abhihutya mukte hiraṇya-retasi tad-dhūma-śamalena sampraviṣṭena mayā asminn eva latā-maṇḍape sthātavyam | tvaṃ punaḥ pragāḍhāyāṃ pradoṣa-velāyām ālapiṣyasi karṇe kṛta-narma-smitā vikaṭa-varmāṇam -- ' dhūrto 'si tvam a=kṛta-jñaś ca | mad-anugraha-labdhena api rūpeṇa loka-locana-utsavāyamānena mat-sapatnīr abhiramayiṣyasi | na aham ātma-vināśāya vetāla-utthāpanam ācareyam ' iti | śrutva īdaṃ tvad-vacaḥ sa yad vadiṣyati tan mahyam ekākiny upāgatya nivedayiṣyasi | tataḥ param aham eva jñāsyāmi | mat-pada-cihnāni ca upavane puṣkarikayā pramārjaya ' iti | sā ' tathā ' iti śāstra-upadeśam iva mad-uktam ādṛtya a=tṛpta-surata-rāga aiva kathaṃ=katham apy agād antaḥ-puram | aham api yathā-praveśaṃ nirgatya svam evā avāsam ayāsiṣam |

atha sā mattakāśinī tathā tam artham anvatiṣṭhat | atiṣṭhac ca tanmate sa durmatiḥ | abhramac ca paurajānapadeṣv iyam adbhutāyamānā vārtā - ' rājā kila vikaṭavarmā devīmantrabalena devayogyaṃ vapur āsādayiṣyati | nūnam eṣa vipralambho na atikalyāṇaḥ | kaiva kathā pramādasya | svasminn eva antaḥpuropavane svāgramahiṣyaiva sampādyaḥ kila ayam arthaḥ | tathā hi bṛhaspatipratimabuddhibhir mantribhir apy abhyūhya anumataḥ | yady evaṃ bhāvi na anyad ataḥ param asti kiñ=cid adbhutam | a=cintyo hi maṇimantrauṣadhīnāṃ prabhāvaḥ | ' iti prasṛteṣu lokapravādeṣu prāpte parvadivase pragāḍhāyāṃ prauḍhatamasi pradoṣavelāyām antaḥpurodyānād udairayad dhūrjaṭikaṇṭhadhūmro dhūmodgamaḥ | kṣīrājyadadhitilagaurasarṣapavasāmāmsarudhira āhutīnāṃ ca parimalaḥ pavanānusārī diśi diśi prāvātsīt | praśānte ca sahasā dhūmodgame tasminn aham aviśam | niśāntodyānam āgamac ca gajagāminī | āliṅgya ca māṃ sasmitaṃ samabhyadhatta - ' dhūrta siddhaṃ te samīhitam | avasitaś ca paśur asau | amuṣya pralobhanāya tvadādiṣṭayā diśā mayoktam - ' kitava na sādhayāmi te saundaryam | evaṃ sundaro hi tvam apsarasām api spṛhaṇīyo bhaviṣyasi kim uta mānuṣīṇām | madhukara iva nisargacapalo yatra kva=cid āsajjati bhavādṛśo nṛśamsaḥ ' iti |
children.translated_text: Then that woman, feigning intoxication (<s>mattakāśinī</s>), carried out the plan accordingly. And that fool abided by her counsel. And this report, causing great wonder, spread among the townspeople and countryfolk: 'King <s>Vikaṭavarman</s>, they say, will attain a body fit for the gods through the power of a divine spell! Surely this is no deception, but something supremely auspicious. What need even to mention carelessness? This matter, they say, is to be accomplished by his own chief queen in the very garden of the inner palace. For even the ministers, whose wisdom rivals <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s, having deliberated, have given their approval. If this is to be, then there is nothing more wondrous than this. Indeed, the power of gems, spells, and herbs is inconceivable.' While such popular talk was spreading, on the appointed festival day, in the deep darkness at the hour of nightfall, from the inner palace garden there rose a column of smoke, dark as the throat of <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). And the fragrance of the oblations — of milk, ghee, curds, sesame, white mustard, fat, flesh, and blood — was carried by the wind in every direction. And when that column of smoke suddenly subsided, I entered. She of the elephant gait came to the night-garden, and embracing me, said with a smile: 'Rogue, your desire is accomplished! And that beast [the king] is done for. To beguile him, at your direction I said: "Gambler! I will not make you handsome. For you are already so handsome that you would be desirable even to <s>Apsarases</s>, to say nothing of mortal women. Fickle as a bee by nature, a heartless one like you would attach himself to anyone at all!"'

tena tu me pādayor nipatya abhihitam - ' rambhoru sahasva matkṛtāni duścaritāni | manasā api na cintayeyam itaḥ param itaranārīm | tvarasva prastute karmaṇi ' iti | tad aham īdṛśena vaivāhikena nepathyena tvām abhisṛtavatī | prāg api rāgāgnisākṣikam anaṅgena guruṇā dattaiva tubhyam eṣā jāyā | punar apīmaṃ jātavedasaṃ sākṣīkṛtya svahṛdayena dattā ' iti prapadena caraṇapṛṣṭhe niṣpīḍyotkṣiptapādapārṣṇir itaretaravyatiṣaktakomalāṅgulidalena bhujalatādvayena kandharāṃ mamāveṣṭya salīlam ānanam ānamayya svayam unnamitamukhakamalā-vibhrāntaviśāladṛṣṭir asakṛd abhyacumbat |
children.translated_text: He then fell at my feet and said: 'O beautiful-thighed one, forgive the misdeeds I have committed! Not even in thought shall I think of another woman hereafter. Make haste with the rite that has been prepared.' So I have come to you in this bridal attire. Even before, with the fire of passion as witness, <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love) himself, the preceptor, had already given this wife to you. And now again, making this sacrificial fire the witness, she is given by her own heart.' With the tip of her toe pressing down upon the top of my foot and her heel raised, with both her vine-like arms — their soft finger-petals interlocked with one another — encircling my neck, playfully bending her face while herself lifting her lotus-face upward, her wide eyes wandering, she kissed me again and again.

kṛtāntadūtīvāhvayantī | prāvartiṣi ca aham agurucandanapramukhāni hotum | āyāsīc ca rājā yathoktam deśam | śaṅkāpannam iva kiñcit savismayaṃ vicārya tiṣṭhantam abravam  ' brūhi satyaṃ bhūyo 'pi me bhagavantaṃ citrabhānum eva sākṣīkṛtya | na ced anena rūpeṇa matsapatnīr abhiramayiṣyasi tatas tvayīdaṃ rūpaṃ saṅkrāmayeyam ' iti | sa tadaiva devy eveyam nopadhiḥ iti sphuṭopajātasampratyayaḥ prāvartata śapathāya | smitvā punar mayoktam  ' kiṃ vā śapathena | kaiva hi mānuṣī māṃ paribhaviṣyati | yady apsarobhiḥ saṅgacchase saṅgacchasva kāmam | kathaya kāni te rahasyāni | tatkathanānte hi tvatsvarūpabhraṃśaḥ ' iti | so 'bravīt  ' asti baddho matpituḥ kanīyān bhrātā prahāravarmā | taṃ viṣānnena vyāpādya ajīrṇadoṣaṃ khyāpayeyam iti mantribhiḥ saha adhyavasitam | anujāya viśālavarmaṇe daṇḍacakraṃ puṇḍradeśābhikramaṇāya ditsitam | pauravṛddhaś ca pāñcālikaḥ paritrātaś ca sārthavāhaḥ khanatināmno yavanād vajram ekaṃ vasundharāmūlyaṃ laghīyasā argheṇa labhyam iti mamaikānte amantrayetām | gṛhapatiś ca mama antaraṅgabhūto janapadamahattaraḥ śatahalir alīkavādaśīlam avalepavantaṃ duṣṭagrāmaṇyam anantasīraṃ janapadakopena ghātayeyam iti daṇḍadharān uddhārakarmaṇi matprayogān niyoktum abhyupāgamat | ittham idam aciraprastutaṃ rahasyam ity ākarṇya tam ' iyat tavāyuḥ | upapadyasva svakarmocitāṃ gatim ' iti cchurikayā dvidhā kṛtya kṛttamātraṃ tasminn eva pravṛttasphītasarpiṣi hiraṇyaretasy ajuhavam | abhūc ca asau bhasmasāt | atha strīsvabhāvād īṣadvihvalāṃ hṛdayavallabhāṃ samāśvāsya hastakisalaye avalambya gatvā tadgṛham anujñayā asyāḥ sarvāṇy antaḥpurāṇy āhūya sadya eva sevāṃ dattavān | savismitavilāsinīsārthamadhye kañcid vihṛtya kālaṃ visṛṣṭāvarodhamaṇḍalas tām eva samhatorūm ūrūpapīḍaṃ bhujopapīḍaṃ copagūhya talpe 'bhiramayann alpām iva tāṃ niśām atyanaiṣam | alabhe ca tanmukhāt tadrājakulasya śīlam | uṣasi snātvā kṛtamaṅgalo mantribhiḥ saha samagacche | tāmś ca abravam - ' āryāḥ rūpeṇaiva saha parivṛtto mama svabhāvaḥ | ya eṣa viṣānnena hantuṃ cintitaḥ pitā me sa muktvā svam etad rājyaṃ bhūya eva grāhayitavyaḥ | pitṛvad amuṣmin vayaṃ śuśrūṣayaiva vartāmahe | na hy asti pitṛvadhāt paraṃ pātakam ' iti | bhrātaraṃ ca viśālavarmāṇam āhūyoktavān - ' vatsa na subhikṣāḥ sāmprataṃ puṇḍrāḥ | te duḥkhamohopahatās tyaktātmāno rāṣṭraṃ naḥ samṛddham abhidraveyuḥ | ato muṣṭivadhaḥ sasyavadho vā yadotpadyate tadā abhiyāsyasi | na adya yātrā yuktā ' iti | nagaravṛddhāv apy alāpiṣam - ' alpīyasā mūlyena mahārhaṃ vajravastu mā astu me labhyaṃ dharmarakṣāyai tadanuguṇenaiva mūlyena adaḥ krīyatām ' iti | śatahaliṃ ca rāṣṭramukhyam āhūya ākhyātavān - ' yo 'sāv anantasīraḥ prahāravarmaṇaḥ pakṣa iti nināśayiṣitaḥ so 'pi pitari me prakṛtisthe kim iti nāśyeta tat tvayā api tasmin samrambho na kāryaḥ ' iti | tae ime sarvam ābhijñānikam upalabhya ' sa eva ayam iti niścinvānā vismayamānāś ca tāṃ mahādevīṃ ca praśamsanto mantrabalāni codghoṣayanto bandhanāt pitarau niṣkrāmayya svaṃ rājyaṃ pratya pādayan | ahaṃ ca tayā me dhātryā sarvam idaṃ mama ceṣṭitaṃ rahasi pitror avagamayya praharṣakāṣṭhādhirūḍhayos tayoḥ pādamūlam abhaje | abhajye ca yauvarājyalakṣmyā tadanujñātayā | prasādhitātmā devapādavirahaduḥkhadurbhagān bhogān nirviśan bhūyo 'sya pitṛsakhasya simhavarmaṇo lekhyāc caṇḍavarmaṇaś campābhiyogam avagamya ' śatruvadho mitrarakṣā cobhayam api karaṇīyam eva ' ity alaghunā laghusamutthānena sainyacakreṇa abhyasaram | abhūvaṃ ca bhūmis tvatpādalakṣmīsākṣātkriyāmahotsavānandarāśeḥ ' iti | śrutvaitad devo rājavāhanaḥ sasmitam avādīt - ' paśyata pāratalpikam upadhiyuktam api gurujanabandhavyasanamuktihetutayā duṣṭā-mitrapramāpaṇābhyupāyatayā rājyopalabdhimūlatayā ca puṣkalāv arthadharmāv apy arīradhat | kiṃ hi buddhimatprayuktaṃ na abhyupaiti śobhām ' iti | arthapālamukhe nidhāya snigdhadīrghāṃ dṛṣṭim ' ācaṣṭāṃ bhavān ātmīyacaritam ' ity ādideśa | so 'pi baddhāñjalir abhidadhe -
children.translated_text: Then, telling her, 'Stay right here, hidden in the <s>kuraṇṭaka</s> thicket, until I go out and properly accomplish what must be accomplished,' I left her and, approaching the area of the sacrificial fire, shook a bell hanging from an <s>aśoka</s> branch. It rang out, as if a messenger of Death summoning that person. I then began to offer <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood), sandalwood, and the like as oblations. The king came to the designated place. Addressing him as he stood there, somewhat apprehensive, looking around with surprise, I said: 'Speak the truth again to me, making the Lord <s>Citrabhānu</s> (Fire) himself the witness. If you will not delight my co-wives with this [beauty] form, then I shall transfer this form onto you.' He, immediately gaining the firm conviction, 'This is truly the queen, not a deception,' proceeded to swear an oath. Smiling, I then said: 'What need is there for an oath? What human woman could ever surpass me? If you consort with <s>Apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), do so as you please. Tell me — what are your secrets? For at the end of their telling, your own true form will be lost.' He said: 'My father's younger brother, <s>Prahāravarman</s>, is imprisoned. The plan devised with the ministers is to kill him with poisoned food and declare it a digestive ailment. The military command is to be given to my younger brother <s>Viśālavarman</s> for a campaign against the <s>Puṇḍra</s> country. The city elder, <s>Pāñcālika</s>, and a protected merchant privately informed me that a single diamond worth the price of the whole earth can be obtained for a lesser price from a <s>Yavana</s> (foreigner) named <s>Khanati</s>. And the householder <s>Śatahali</s>, a chief of the countryside and an intimate of mine, approached me to appoint his enforcers for the task of destruction, saying: "I should have the wicked village headman <s>Anantasīra</s>, who is given to false speech and arrogance, killed by popular outrage." This is the recently devised secret.' Having heard this, I said to him: 'This is the extent of your life. Attain a destiny befitting your own deeds,' and cut him in two with a knife. The very moment he was cut, I offered him as an oblation in that very fire flowing with abundant ghee, the golden-seed fire. And he was reduced to ashes. Then, having comforted my beloved, who was slightly agitated due to feminine nature, I took her by her tender hand and went to his residence. With her permission, I summoned all the women of the inner apartments and immediately accepted their service. Having spent some time amidst the assembly of astonished court-ladies, after dismissing the harem circle, I embraced that very same beautiful-thighed one — pressing thigh against thigh and arm against arm — and, delighting her upon the bed, passed that night which seemed all too brief. And from her lips I learned the character of that royal family. At dawn, having bathed and performed auspicious rites, I met with the ministers and addressed them: 'Noble sirs, my very nature has changed along with my form. He who was planned to be killed with poisoned food — my father — he should be released and made to rule this kingdom once more. We shall attend upon him with filial devotion. For there is no sin greater than patricide.' And summoning his brother <s>Viśālavarman</s>, I said: 'My boy, the <s>Puṇḍras</s> are not prosperous at present. Afflicted by suffering and delusion, having abandoned self-regard, they might attack our flourishing realm. Therefore, when there arises a threat of armed conflict or crop destruction, then you shall march forth. A campaign now is not advisable.' To the city elders too I said: 'Let not a priceless diamond be obtained by me for a trifling price. For the protection of <s>dharma</s>, let it be purchased at a price befitting its value.' And summoning the district chief <s>Śatahali</s>, I declared: 'That <s>Anantasīra</s> who was to be destroyed as a partisan of <s>Prahāravarman</s> — now that my father is restored to his natural position, why should he be destroyed? Therefore, you too should harbor no hostility toward him.' Then these men, recognizing all this as [evidence of] the supernatural, convinced that 'this is indeed he,' and filled with wonder, praising the great queen and proclaiming the power of <s>mantras</s>, released the parents from prison and restored them to their own kingdom. And I, having that nurse of mine reveal all my deeds privately to the parents — who were transported to the pinnacle of delight — attended at their feet. And I was consecrated in the dignity of crown-prince by their command. Having adorned myself, experiencing pleasures — though rendered unfortunate by the sorrow of separation from the Lord [<s>Rājavāhana</s>] — I later learned from a letter of <s>Siṃhavarman</s>, my father's friend, about <s>Caṇḍavarman's</s> attack on <s>Campā</s>. Thinking, 'The destruction of an enemy and the protection of a friend — both must be accomplished,' with no small force and swift mobilization, I marched forth with an army. And I arrived at this land, [a place] for the great festival of joy at the direct vision of the glory of your feet.' Having heard this, the Lord <s>Rājavāhana</s> said with a smile: 'See — adultery, even when combined with deception, produced abundant results in both wealth and <s>dharma</s>, being the cause of liberation from the affliction of imprisoning kinsmen, the means of destroying a wicked enemy, and the foundation for obtaining a kingdom. What deed, when employed by the intelligent, does not attain splendor?' Resting his affectionate, lingering gaze upon <s>Arthapāla's</s> face, he commanded: 'Sir, recount your own story.' And he too, with palms joined, began to speak —

akūjac ca sā taṃ janaṃ kṛtānta-dūti īvā ahvayantī | prāvartiṣi ca aham a-guru-candana-pramukhāni hotum | āyāsīc ca rājā yathā-uktam deśam | śaṅkā-āpannam iva kiñ-cit sa-vismayaṃ vicārya tiṣṭhantam abravam - ' brūhi satyaṃ bhūyo 'pi me bhagavantaṃ citra-bhānum eva sākṣīkṛtya | na ced anena rūpeṇa mat-sapatnīr abhiramayiṣyasi tatas tvayi idaṃ rūpaṃ saṅkrāmayeyam ' iti | sa tada aiva devy eva iyam na upadhiḥ iti sphuṭa-upajāta-sampratyayaḥ prāvartata śapathāya | smitvā punar maya ūktam - ' kiṃ vā śapathena | ka aiva hi mānuṣī māṃ paribhaviṣyati | yady apsarobhiḥ saṅgacchase saṅgacchasva kāmam | kathaya kāni te rahasyāni | tat-kathana-ante hi tvat-sva-rūpa-bhraṃśaḥ ' iti | so 'bravīt - ' asti baddho mat-pituḥ kanīyān bhrātā prahāra-varmā | taṃ viṣa-annena vyāpādya a-jīrṇa-doṣaṃ khyāpayeyam iti mantribhiḥ saha adhyavasitam | anujāya viśāla-varmaṇe daṇḍa-cakraṃ puṇḍra-deśa-abhikramaṇāya ditsitam | paura-vṛddhaś ca pāñcālikaḥ paritrātaś ca sārtha-vāhaḥ khanati-nāmno yavanād vajram ekaṃ vasundharā-mūlyaṃ laghīyasā argheṇa labhyam iti mama ekānte amantrayetām | gṛha-patiś ca mama antaraṅga-bhūto janapada-mahattaraḥ śata-halir alīka-vāda-śīlam avalepavantaṃ duṣṭa-grāmaṇyam ananta-sīraṃ janapada-kopena ghātayeyam iti daṇḍa-dharān uddhāra-karmaṇi mat-prayogān niyoktum abhyupāgamat | ittham idam a-cira-prastutaṃ rahasyam ity ākarṇya tam ' iyat tavā ayuḥ | upapadyasva sva-karma-ucitāṃ gatim ' iti cchurikayā dvidhā kṛtya kṛtta-mātraṃ tasminn eva pravṛtta-sphīta-sarpiṣi hiraṇya-retasy ajuhavam | abhūc ca asau bhasmasāt | atha strī-svabhāvād īṣad-vihvalāṃ hṛdaya-vallabhāṃ samāśvāsya hasta-kisalaye avalambya gatvā tad-gṛham anujñayā asyāḥ sarvāṇy antaḥ-purāṇy āhūya sadya eva sevāṃ dattavān | sa-vismita-vilāsinī-sārtha-madhye kañ-cid vihṛtya kālaṃ visṛṣṭa-avarodha-maṇḍalas tām eva samhata-ūrūm ūru-upapīḍaṃ bhuja-upapīḍaṃ ca upagūhya talpe 'bhiramayann alpām iva tāṃ niśām atyanaiṣam | alabhe ca tan-mukhāt tad-rāja-kulasya śīlam | uṣasi snātvā kṛta-maṅgalo mantribhiḥ saha samagacche | tāmś ca abravam -- ' āryāḥ rūpeṇa eva saha parivṛtto mama svabhāvaḥ | ya eṣa viṣa-annena hantuṃ cintitaḥ pitā me sa muktvā svam etad rājyaṃ bhūya eva grāhayitavyaḥ | pitṛvad amuṣmin vayaṃ śuśrūṣaya aiva vartāmahe | na hy asti pitṛ-vadhāt paraṃ pātakam ' iti | bhrātaraṃ ca viśāla-varmāṇam āhūya uktavān -- ' vatsa na su-bhikṣāḥ sāmprataṃ puṇḍrāḥ | te duḥkha-moha-upahatās tyakta-ātmāno rāṣṭraṃ naḥ samṛddham abhidraveyuḥ | ato muṣṭi-vadhaḥ sasya-vadho vā yada ūtpadyate tadā abhiyāsyasi | na adya yātrā yuktā ' iti | nagara-vṛddhāv apy alāpiṣam -- ' alpīyasā mūlyena mahā-arhaṃ vajra-vastu mā astu me labhyaṃ dharma-rakṣāyai tad-anuguṇena eva mūlyena adaḥ krīyatām ' iti | śata-haliṃ ca rāṣṭra-mukhyam āhūya ākhyātavān -- ' yo 'sāv ananta-sīraḥ prahāra-varmaṇaḥ pakṣa iti nināśayiṣitaḥ so 'pi pitari me prakṛti-sthe kim iti nāśyeta tat tvayā api tasmin samrambho na kāryaḥ ' iti | tae ime sarvam ābhijñānikam upalabhya ' sa eva ayam iti niścinvānā vismayamānāś ca tāṃ mahā-devīṃ ca praśamsanto mantra-balāni ca udghoṣayanto bandhanāt pitarau niṣkrāmayya svaṃ rājyaṃ pratya pādayan | ahaṃ ca tayā me dhātryā sarvam idaṃ mama ceṣṭitaṃ rahasi pitror avagamayya praharṣa-kāṣṭhā-adhirūḍhayos tayoḥ pāda-mūlam abhaje | abhajye ca yauvarājya-lakṣmyā tad-anujñātayā | prasādhita-ātmā deva-pāda-viraha-duḥkha-durbhagān bhogān nirviśan bhūyo 'sya pitṛ-sakhasya simha-varmaṇo lekhyāc caṇḍa-varmaṇaś campā-abhiyogam avagamya ' śatru-vadho mitra-rakṣā ca ubhayam api karaṇīyam eva ' ity a-laghunā laghu-samutthānena sainya-cakreṇa abhyasaram | abhūvaṃ ca bhūmis tvat-pāda-lakṣmī-sākṣāt-kriyā-mahā-utsava-ānanda-rāśeḥ ' iti | śrutva aitad devo rāja-vāhanaḥ sa-smitam avādīt -- ' paśyata pāra-talpikam upadhi-yuktam api guru-jana-bandha-vyasana-mukti-hetutayā duṣṭa-a-mitra-pramāpaṇa-abhyupāyatayā rājya-upalabdhi-mūlatayā ca puṣkalāv artha-dharmāv apy arīradhat | kiṃ hi buddhimat-prayuktaṃ na abhyupaiti śobhām ' iti | artha-pāla-mukhe nidhāya snigdha-dīrghāṃ dṛṣṭim ' ācaṣṭāṃ bhavān ātmīya-caritam ' ity ādideśa | so 'pi baddha-añjalir abhidadhe --
/ iti śrīdaṇḍinaḥ kṛtau daśa-kumāra-caritae upahāra-varma caritaṃ nāma tṛtīya ucchvāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Daśakumāracarita</s> (Tale of the Ten Princes) composed by the glorious <s>Daṇḍin</s>, [this is] the third chapter, named 'The Story of <s>Upahāravarman</s>.'

children.text: / pañcama ucchvāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fifth Chapter

children.text: so 'pi praṇamya vijñāpayāmāsa  ' deva devasya anveṣaṇāya dikṣu bhramann abhraṃkaṣasya api vindhyapārśvarūḍhasya vanaspater adhaḥ pariṇatapataṅgabālapallavāvatamsite paścimadigaṅganāmukhe palvalāmbhasy upaspṛśyopāsya sandhyāṃ tamaḥsamīkṛteṣu nimnonnateṣu gantum akṣamaḥ kṣamātale kisalayair uparacayya śayyāṃ śiśayiṣamāṇaḥ śirasi kurvann añjalim ' yā asmin vanaspatau vasati devatā saiva me śaraṇam astu śarārucakracārabhīṣaṇāyāṃ śarvagalaśyāmaśārvarāndhakārapūrādhmātagabhīragahvarāyām asyāṃ mahāṭavyām ekakasya me prasuptasya ' ity upadhāya vāmabhujam aśayiṣi | tataḥ kṣaṇād eva avanidurlabhena sparśena asu khāyiṣata kim āpa gātrāṇi āhlādayiṣatendriyāṇi abhyamanāyiṣṭa ca antarātmā viśeṣataś ca hṛṣitās tanūruhāḥ paryasphuran me dakṣiṇabhujaḥ | ' kathaṃ nv idam ' iti mandamandam unmiṣann upary acchacandrātapacchedakalpaṃ śuklāmśukavitānam aikṣiṣi | vāmato valitadṛṣṭiḥ samayā saudhabhittiṃ citrāstaraṇaśāyinam ativiśrabdhaprasuptam aṅganājanam alakṣayam | dakṣiṇato dattacakṣur āgalitastanāmśukām amṛtaphenapaṭalapāṇḍuraśayanaśāyinīm ādivarāhadamṣṭrāmśujālalagnām amsasrastadugdhasāgaradukūlottarīyāṃ bhayasādhvasamūrchitām iva dharaṇīm aruṇādharakiraṇabālakisalayalāsyahetubhir ānanāravindaparimalodvāhibhir niḥśvāsamātariśvabhir īśvarekṣaṇadahanadagdhaṃ sphuliṅgaśeṣam anaṅgam iva sandhukṣayantīm antaḥsuptaṣaṭpadam ambujam iva jātanidraṃ sarasam āmīlitalocanendīvaram ānanaṃ dadhānām airāvatamadāvalepalūnāpaviddhām iva nandanavanakalpavṛkṣaratnavallarīm kām api taruṇīm ālokayam | atarkayaṃ ca  ' kva gatā sā mahāṭavī kuta idam ūrdhvāṇḍakapālasaṃ puṭodarollekhi śaktidhvajaśikharaśūlotsedhaṃ saudham āgatam kva ca tadaraṇyasthalīsamāstīrṇaṃ pallavaśayanam kutastyaṃ cedam indugabhastisambhārabhāsuraṃ hamsatūladukūlaśayanam | eṣa ca ko nu śītaraśmikiraṇarajjudolāparibhraṣṭamūrchita iva apsarogaṇaḥ svairasuptaḥ sundarījanaḥ kā ceyaṃ devīva aravindahastā śāradaśaśāṅkamaṇḍalāmaladukūlottaracchadam adhiśete śayanatalam | na tāvad eṣā devayoṣā yato mandamandam indukiraṇaiḥ samvāhyamānā kamalinīva saṅkucati | bhagnavṛntacyutarasabinduśabalitaṃ pākapāṇḍucūtaphalam ivodbhinnasvedarekham ālakṣyate gaṇḍasthalam | abhinavayauvanavidāhanirbharoṣmaṇi kucataṭe vaivarṇyam upaiti varṇakam | vāsasī ca paribhogānurūpaṃ dhūsarimāṇam ādarśayataḥ | tad eṣā mānuṣy eva | diṣṭyā ca anucchiṣṭayauvanā yataḥ saukumāryam āgatāḥ samhatā iva avayavāḥ prasnigdhatamā api pāṇḍutānuviddheva dehacchaviḥ dantapīḍānabhijñatayā na ativiśadarāgo mukhe vidrumadyutir adharamaṇiḥ anatyāpūrṇam āraktamūlaṃ campakakuḍmaladalam iva kaṭhoraṃ kapolatalam anaṅgabāṇapātamuktāśaṅkaṃ ca viśrabdhamadhuraṃ supyate na caitadvakṣaḥsthalaṃ nirdayavimardavistāritamukhastanayugalam asti ca anati krāntaśiṣṭamaryādacetaso mama asyām āsaktiḥ | āsaktyanurūpaṃ punar āśliṣṭā yadi spaṣṭam ārtaraveṇaiva saha nidrāṃ mokṣyati | atha ahaṃ na śakṣyāmi ca anupaśliṣya śayitum | ato yad bhāvi tad bhavatu | bhāgyam atra parīkṣiṣye | ' iti spṛṣṭā-spṛṣṭam eva kim apy āviddharāgasādhvasaṃ lakṣyasuptaḥ sthito 'smi | sā api kim apy utkampinā romodbhedavatā vāmapārśvena sukhāyamānena mandamandajṛmbhitakārambhamantharāṅgī tvaṅgadagrapakṣmaṇoś cakṣuṣor alasatāntatārakeṇa anatipakvanidrākaṣāyitāpāṅgaparabhāgeṇa yugaleneṣad unmilantī trāsavismayaharṣarāgaśaṅkāvilāsavibhramavyavahitāni vrīḍāntarāṇi kāni kāny api kāmena adbhutānubhāvena avasthāntarāṇi kāryamāṇā parijanaprabodhanodyatā giraṃ kāmāvegaparavaśaṃ hṛdayam aṅgāni ca sādhvasāyāsasambadhyamānasvedapulakāni kathaṃ katham api nigṛhya saspṛheṇa madhurakūṇitatribhāgeṇa mandamandapracāritena cakṣuṣā madaṅgāni nirvarṇya dūrotsarpitapūrvakāyā api tasminn eva śayane sacakitam aśayiṣṭa | ajaniṣṭa me rāgāviṣṭacetaso 'pi kim api nidrā | punar ananukūlasparśaduḥkhāyattagātraḥ prābudhye | prabuddhasya ca me saiva mahāṭavī tad eva tarutalaṃ sa eva patrāstaro 'bhūt | vibhāvarī ca vyabhāsīt | abhūc ca me manasi  ' kim ayaṃ svapnaḥ kiṃ vipralambho vā kim iyam āsurī daivī vā kā api māyā | yad bhāvi tad bhavatu | na aham idaṃ tatvato na avabudhya mokṣyāmi bhūmiśayyām | yāvadāyur atratyāyai devatāyai pratiśayito bhavāmi ' iti niścitamatir atiṣṭham |
children.translated_text: He too, having bowed, made his report: 'My lord, while wandering about the regions in search of my lord, beneath a forest tree that, rooted on the slope of the <s>Vindhya</s>, scraped the very clouds, in the western quarter—the face of that celestial maiden adorned with the young sprouts where the tilting sun had ripened—having touched the water of a pool, having worshipped the twilight, and being unable to go on amid the high and low places now leveled into darkness, I prepared a couch of tender shoots upon the surface of the earth, and, wishing to sleep, making an añjali upon my head, [I prayed:] "May that very deity who dwells in this forest tree be my refuge in this great wilderness—dreadful with the wheeling course of beasts of prey, its deep hollows swollen with a flood of nocturnal darkness black as <s>Śarva</s>'s throat—for me, sleeping here alone"—and so, pillowing my left arm, I lay down. Then in but a moment, by a touch hard to find upon the earth, my breath grew easy, somehow my limbs were soothed, my senses were gladdened, and my inner self was refreshed; and especially the hairs upon my body bristled, and my right arm throbbed. 'How can this be?' [I thought,] and opening my eyes ever so slowly, I beheld above me a canopy of white cloth like a stretch of clear moonlight. Glancing to my left, near a plastered wall, I made out a company of women sleeping most trustfully upon figured spreads. Casting my eyes to the right, I beheld some young woman: her bodice slipped from her breast, lying upon a couch pale as a mass of nectar-foam, caught in the net of rays from the tusk of the Primeval Boar, her silken upper-garment slipped from her shoulder like the ocean-of-milk garment of the Earth, [seeming] as if swooning with terror like the Earth herself—bearing a lotus-face whose lotus-eyes were closed, like a fresh lotus with sleeping bees within, like Love [<s>Anaṅga</s>], scorched to ashes by the eye-fire of <s>Īśvara</s> with only sparks remaining, being fanned back [to life] by the breaths that, wafting the fragrance of her lotus-face, danced upon her tender-sprout red lower lip. And I reasoned: 'Where has that great wilderness gone? Whence has come this mansion, its dome's belly etched [with carving], rising to the height of spear-points, banners, and pinnacles? And where is that bed of sprouts spread upon the forest floor? And whence is this couch, brilliant with the mass of moonbeams, of swan's-down and fine silk? And who is this company of fair women, sleeping at their ease like a host of <s>apsarases</s> fallen swooning from the swing-ropes of the cool-rayed moon? And who is this lady, like a goddess with a lotus in her hand, who lies upon the bed whose coverlet is spotless silk like the disc of the autumn moon? She is not, at any rate, a celestial woman, for, slowly being stroked by the moon's rays, she contracts like a lotus-plant. Her cheek, dappled like a sap-drop fallen from a broken stalk upon a mango-fruit ripened pale, shows a line of welling sweat. Upon the slope of her breast, with the fierce heat of fresh youth's burning, the cosmetic paint loses its color. And her two garments display a dinginess befitting use. So she is indeed a mortal woman. And by good fortune her youth is untasted, for, by reason of her tenderness, her limbs seem as if drawn together, the hue of her body, though most glossy, is as if shot through with pallor, the lip-gem upon her mouth has the coral-luster not over-vivid, unfamiliar with the bruising of teeth, her cheek-region, hard like a champaka bud not fully opened, reddish at its base, and this bosom is not split open by the arrow-stroke of Love—it sleeps trustfully and sweetly, this pair of breasts not spread wide by ruthless crushing. And there arises in me, whose mind has not transgressed the bounds of the well-bred, an attachment to her. But this attachment being requited, were I to embrace her, plainly she would wake from sleep with a cry of distress. And then I shall not be able to lie down without drawing close to her. Therefore, let what is to be, be; here I shall test my fortune.' And so, touching and not-touching, with some flush of agitated passion, I remained feigning sleep. And she too, with her left side somewhat trembling, thrilled with horripilation and soothed [by my touch], her body languid with the slow, churning sluggishness of waking yawns, slightly opening her pair of eyes whose dark pupils were languid at the corners, their outer edges stained as if by sleep not yet fully ripe, being made by Love—whose power is wondrous—to pass through various conditions, certain unspeakable inner states of bashfulness pierced through with fear, astonishment, joy, passion, doubt, dalliance, and flutter; [and] her voice eager to wake the attendants, her heart helpless under the surge of love, and her limbs joined with sweat and horripilation born of agitation and toil—all these somehow restraining, with a longing eye sweetly half-shut at the corners, slowly moving, she scanned my limbs; and though she drew the upper part of her body far away, yet upon that very couch she lay down again, startled. And there came upon me too, though my mind was filled with passion, some sleep. Then again, my limbs made wretched by an uncongenial touch, I awoke. And when I had awoken, that same great wilderness, that same foot of a tree, that same spread of leaves [were before me]. And the night had passed [into day]. And it arose in my mind: 'Is this a dream? Or some deception? Or is it some demonic or divine illusion? Let what is to be, be. I shall not, without truly understanding this, abandon this earthen bed. As long as I have life, I shall lie down here in supplication to the deity of this place'—and so, with resolved mind, I remained.'
