dvi-trān upa-damśān upapādya tad-anna-maṇḍam ārdra-vālukā-upahita-nava-śarāva-gatam ati-mṛdunā tāla-vṛnta-anilena śītalīkṛtya sa-lavaṇa-sambhāraṃ datta-aṅgāra-dhūpa-vāsaṃ ca sampādya tad apy āmalakaṃ ślakṣṇa-piṣṭam utpala-gandhi kṛtvā dhātrī-mukhena snā nāya tam acodayat | tayā ca snāna-śuddhayā datta-taila-āmalakaḥ krameṇa sasnau | snātaḥ sikta-mṛṣṭe kuṭṭime phalakam āruhya pāṇḍu-haritasya tri-bhāga-śeṣa-lūnasya aṅgaṇa-kadalī-palāśasya upari śarāva-dvayaṃ dattam ārdram abhimṛśann atiṣṭhat | sā tu tāṃ peyām eva agre samupāharat | pītvā ca apanata-adhva-klamaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ praklinna-sakala-gātraḥ sthito 'bhūt | tatas tasya śāly-odanasya darvī-dvayaṃ datvā sarpir-mā trāṃ sūpam upa-damśaṃ ca upajahāra | imaṃ ca dadhnā ca tri-jātaka-avacūrṇitena surabhi-śītalābhyāṃ ca kālaśeya-kāñjikābhyāṃ śeṣam annam abhojayat | sa-śeṣae eva andhasy asāv atṛpyat | ayācata ca pānīyam | atha nava-bhṛṅgāra-sambhṛtam aguru-dhūpa-dhūpitam abhinava-pāṭalī-kusuma-vāsitam utphulla-utpala-grathita-saurabhaṃ vāri nālī-dhārā-ātmanā pātayāṃ babhūva | so 'pi mukha-upahita-śarāveṇa hima-śiśira-kaṇa-karālita-aruṇāyamāna-akṣi-pakṣmā dhārā-rava-abhinandita-śravaṇaḥ sparśa-sukha-udbhinna-romāñca-karkaśa-kapolaḥ parimala-pravāla-utpīḍa-phulla-ghrāṇa-randhro mādhurya-prakarṣa-āvarjita-rasanā-indriyas tad acchaṃ pānīyam ā-kaṇṭhaṃ papau | śiraḥ-kampa-saṃjñā-vāritā ca punar apara-karakeṇā acamanam adatta kanyā | vṛddhayā tu tad-ucchiṣṭam apohya harita-gomaya-upalipte kuṭṭime svam eva uttarīya-karpaṭaṃ vyavadhāya kṣaṇam aśeta | parituṣṭaś ca vidhivad upayamya kanyāṃ ninye | nītva aitad-an-apekṣaḥ kām=api gaṇikām avarodham akarot | tām apy asau priya-sakhīm iva upācarat | patiṃ ca daivatam iva mukta-tandrā paryacarat | gṛha-kāryāṇi ca a-hīnam anvatiṣṭhat | parijanaṃ ca dākṣiṇya-nidhir ātma-adhīnam akarot | tad-guṇa-vaśīkṛtaś ca bhartā sarvam eva kuṭumbaṃ tad-āyattam eva kṛtvā tad-eka-adhīna-jīvita-śarīras tri-vargaṃ nirviveśa | tad bravīmi --' gṛhiṇaḥ priya-hitāya dāra-guṇāḥ ' iti |

tatas tena anuyukto nimbavatīvṛttam ākhyātavān - ' asti saurāṣṭreṣu valabhī nāma nagarī | tasyāṃ gṛhaguptanāmno guhyakendratulyavibhavasya nāvikapater duhitā ratnavatī nāma | tāṃ kila madhumatyāḥ samupāgamya balabhadro nāma sārthavāhaputraḥ paryaṇaiṣīt | tayā api navavadhvā rahasi rabhasavighnitasuratasukho jhaṭiti dveṣam alpetaraṃ babandha | na tāṃ punar draṣṭum iṣṭavān | tadgṛhāgamanam api suhṛdvākyaśatātivartī lajjayā parijahāra | tāṃ ca durbhagāṃ tadāprabhṛty eva ' neyaṃ ratnavatī nimbavatī ceyam iti svajanaḥ parajanaś ca paribabhūva | gate ca kasmimś=cit kāle sā tv anutapyamānā ' kā me gatiḥ iti vimṛśantī kām api vṛddhapravrājikāṃ mātṛsthānīyāṃ devaśeṣakusumair upasthitām apaśyat | tasyāḥ puro rahasi sakaruṇaṃ ruroda | tayā apy udaśrumukhyā bahuprakāram anunīya ruditakāraṇaṃ pṛṣṭā trapamāṇā api kāryagauravāt kathañ=cid abravīt - ' amba kiṃ bravīmi | daurbhāgyaṃ nāma jīvanmaraṇam eva aṅganānām viśeṣataś ca kulavadhūnām | tasya aham asmy udāharaṇabhūtā | mātṛpramukho 'pi jñātivargo mām avajñayaiva paśyati | tena sudṛṣṭāṃ māṃ kuru | na cet tyajeyam adyaiva niṣprayojanān prāṇān | ā virāmāc ca me rahasyaṃ nāśrāvyam ' iti pādayoḥ papāta | sainām utthāpyodbāṣpovāca - ' vatse mā adhyavasyaḥ sāhasam | iyam asmi tvannideśavartinī | yāvati mamopayogas tava tāvati bhavāmy ananyādhīnā | yady eva asi nirviṇṇā tapaś cara tvaṃ madadhiṣṭhitā pāralaukikāya kalyāṇāya | nanv ayam udarkaḥ prāktanasya duṣkṛtasya yadanenākāreṇedṛśena śīlena jātyā caivaṃbhūtayā samanugatā saty akasmād eva bhartṛdveṣyatāṃ gatā asi | yadi kaś=cid asty upāyaḥ patidrohapratikriyāyai darśaya amum | matir hi te paṭīyasī ' iti | atha asau kathañ=cit kṣaṇam adhomukhī dhyātvā dīrghoṣṇaśvāsapūrvam avocat - ' bhagavati patir eva daivataṃ vanitānām viśeṣataś ca kulajānām | atas tacchuśrūṣaṇābhyupāyahetubhūtaṃ kiñ=cid ācaraṇīyam | asty asmatprātiveśyo vaṇik | abhijanena vibhavena rājāntaraṅgabhāvena ca sarvapaurān atītya vartate | tasya kanyā kanakavatī nāma matsamānarūpāvayavā mama atisnigdhā sakhī | tayā saha tadvimānaharmyatale tato 'pi dviguṇamaṇḍitā vihariṣyāmi | tvayā tu tanmātṛprārthanaṃ sakaruṇam abhidhāya matpatir etadgṛhaṃ kathañ=canāneyaḥ | samīpagateṣu ca yuṣmāsu krīḍāmattā nāma kandukaṃ bhramśayeyam | atha tam ādāya tasya haste datvā vakṣyasi - ' putra taveyaṃ bhāryāsakhī nidhipatidattasya sarvaśreṣṭhimukhyasya kanyā kanakavatī nāma | tvām iyam anavastho niṣkaruṇaś ceti ratnavatīnimittam atyarthaṃ nindati | tad eṣa kanduko vipakṣadhanaṃ pratyarpaṇīyam ' iti | sa tathokto niyatam unmukhībhūya tām eva priyasakhīṃ manyamāno mām baddhāñjali yācamānāyai mahyaṃ bhūyas tvatprārthitaḥ sābhilāṣam arpayiṣyati | tena randhreṇopaśliṣya rāgam ujjvalīkṛtya yathā asau kṛtasaṅketo deśāntaram ādāya māṃ gamiṣyati tathopapādanīyam ' iti | harṣābhyupetayā ca anayā tathaiva sampāditam | athaitām kanakavatīti vṛddhatāpasīpralabdho balabhadraḥ saratnasārābharaṇām ādāya niśi nīrandhre tamasi prāvasat | sā tu tāpasī vārtām āpādayat - ' mandena mayā nirnimittam upekṣitā ratnavatī śvaśurau ca paribhūtau suhṛdaś ca ativartitāḥ | tad atraiva samsṛṣṭo jīvituṃ jihremīti balabhadraḥ pūrvedyur mām akathayat | nūnam asau tena nītā vyaktiś ca acirād bhaviṣyati iti | tac chrutvā tadbāndhavās tadanveṣaṇaṃ prati śithilayatnās tasthuḥ | ratnavatī tu mārge kāñ=cit paṇyadāsīṃ saṅgṛhya tayohyamānapātheyādyupaskarā kheṭakapuram agamat | amutra ca vyavahārakuśalo balabhadraḥ svalpenaiva mūlena mahaddhanam upārjayat | paurāgragaṇyaś cāsīt | parijanaś ca bhūyān arthavaśāt samājagāma | tatas tāṃ prathamadāsīṃ ' na karma karoṣi dṛṣṭaṃ muṣṇāsi apriyaṃ bravīṣi ' iti paruṣam uktvā bahv atāḍayat | ceṭī tu prasādakālopakhyātarahasyasya vṛttāntaikadeśam āttaroṣā nirbibheda | tac chrutvā tu lubdhena daṇḍavāhinā pauravṛddhasamnidhau ' nidhipatidattasya kanyāṃ kanakavatīṃ moṣeṇa apahṛtya asmatpure nivasaty eṣa durmatir balabhadraḥ | tasya sarvasvaharaṇaṃ bhavadbhir na pratibandhanīyam ' iti nitarām abhartsayata | bhītaṃ ca balabhadram adhijagāda ratnavatī - ' na bhetavyam | brūhi - neyaṃ nidhipatidattakanyā kanakavatī | valabhyām eva gṛhaguptaduhitā ratnavatī nāmeyaṃ dattā pitṛbhyāṃ mayā ca nyāyoḍhā | na cet pratītha praṇidhiṃ prahiṇuta asyā bandhupārśvam ' iti | balabhadras tu tathoktvā śreṇīprātibhāvyena tāvad eva atiṣṭhad yāvat tatpuralekhyalabdhavṛttānto gṛhaguptaḥ kheṭakapuram āgatya saha jāmātrā duhitaram atiprītaḥ pratyanaiṣīt | tathā dṛṣṭvā ratnavatī kanakavatīti bhāvayatas tasyaiva bhalabhadrasya ativallabhā jātā | tad bravīmi - ' kāmo nāma saṅkalpaḥ ' iti |
children.translated_text: Then, when questioned by him, he narrated the story of <s>Nimbavatī</s>: 'In <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> there is a city called <s>Valabhī</s>. In that city, a ship-captain named <s>Gṛhagupta</s>, equal in wealth to the lord of the <s>Guhyakas</s> (<s>Kubera</s>), had a daughter named <s>Ratnavatī</s>. A caravan-leader's son named <s>Balabhadra</s>, having approached [the family] through [the matchmaker] <s>Madhumatī</s>, sought her hand in marriage. But the newly-wed bride, in their private [wedding night], disrupted the pleasure of love-making with her impetuousness, and he at once conceived no small hatred for her. He did not wish to see her again. Even visiting her family's house, defying the words of a hundred well-wishers, he abandoned out of shame. And from that time onward, her own people and strangers alike mocked the unfortunate woman, [saying]: "She is not <s>Ratnavatī</s> (Jewel-Woman) — she is <s>Nimbavatī</s> (Neem-Woman)." After some time had passed, she, burning with remorse and wondering, "What is to become of me?" caught sight of a certain old female ascetic (<s>pravrājikā</s>) who stood in the place of a mother to her, who had come bearing the leftover flowers from a deity's worship. In the privacy of that woman's presence, she wept pitifully. And she, her face streaming with tears, having consoled her in many ways, asked the reason for her weeping. Though ashamed, compelled by the gravity of the matter, <s>Ratnavatī</s> managed to say: "Mother, what can I say? Ill fortune is nothing less than a living death for women, and especially for women of good family. And I am the very embodiment of that truth. Even my own kinfolk, beginning with my mother, look upon me with nothing but contempt. Therefore, make him look upon me with favor. If not, this very day I shall cast off these useless lives. And until the matter is concluded, my secret must not be disclosed to anyone." So saying, she fell at her feet. The old woman raised her up and said, her eyes brimming with tears: "My child, do not resolve upon a rash act. Here I am, ready to follow your command. To whatever extent I can be of service to you, to that extent I shall be at your disposal and no one else's. But if you are truly despairing, then practice austerities under my guidance, for the sake of merit in the next world. For surely this is the ripened fruit of evil deeds committed in a former life — that you, endowed with such beauty, such virtue, such birth, have inexplicably fallen into the state of being hated by your husband. If there is any stratagem to counteract your husband's aversion, show it to me, for your intelligence is keener than mine." Then <s>Ratnavatī</s>, sitting with her face downcast for a moment in thought, preceded by a long, hot sigh, said: "Holy one, a husband is indeed the deity of women, especially of those born in good families. Therefore, something must be done that will serve as the means for gaining his affection. There is a merchant in our neighborhood. In lineage, wealth, and intimacy with the king, he surpasses all the townspeople. His daughter, named <s>Kanakavatī</s>, of the same beauty and figure as myself, is my most intimate friend. Together with her, upon the terrace of her mansion, adorned twice as splendidly, I shall disport myself. Meanwhile, you must bring my husband to her house somehow, by making a piteous appeal to her mother. And when you all draw near, I — pretending to be absorbed in play — shall let a ball drop from my hands. Then, picking up the ball and placing it in his hand, you shall say: 'My son, this is the friend of your wife — the daughter of <s>Nidhipatidatta</s>, the foremost of all guild-masters, named <s>Kanakavatī</s>. She denounces you most bitterly on <s>Ratnavatī</s>'s behalf, calling you faithless and heartless. So here is this ball — a rival's stake that must be returned.' He, thus addressed, will certainly look up with curiosity; and regarding that very dear friend to be [<s>Kanakavatī</s>], he will eagerly offer me — as I stand with palms joined in supplication — to me again, at your further entreaty. Through that opening, having embraced him and kindled his passion, you must arrange matters so that he, having made a secret pact, will take me away to another land." And the old woman, overjoyed, brought it all to pass exactly as described. Then <s>Balabhadra</s>, deceived by the old ascetic into believing this was <s>Kanakavatī</s>, took her — adorned with jewelry rich in gems — and departed with her in the dead of night, in impenetrable darkness. Meanwhile, the ascetic spread the story: "The fool! Without cause I had neglected <s>Ratnavatī</s>, insulted my parents-in-law, and defied my friends. I am ashamed to live in this very place, entangled as I am" — so <s>Balabhadra</s> had told me the day before. "Surely he has taken her away, and confirmation will come before long." Hearing this, her kinsmen, their efforts to search for her grown slack, remained idle. <s>Ratnavatī</s>, meanwhile, having taken along a certain slave-woman for sale on the road, supplied with provisions and necessities by that woman, traveled to the town of <s>Kheṭaka</s>. There, <s>Balabhadra</s>, shrewd in business, earned great wealth with but a small capital, and became the foremost among the townspeople. A large retinue also gathered around him, drawn by his prosperity. Then he harshly scolded that first slave-woman — "You do no work, you steal in plain sight, you speak insolently" — and beat her severely. But the slave-girl, in a fit of rage, revealed part of the secret that had come to be known to her through an occasion of [seeking] favor. Upon hearing this, a greedy magistrate (<s>daṇḍavāhin</s>), in the presence of the town elders, furiously denounced him: "This wicked <s>Balabhadra</s> has abducted by theft the daughter of <s>Nidhipatidatta</s>, the girl <s>Kanakavatī</s>, and is living in our city. His entire property should be confiscated, and you ought not to prevent it." And <s>Ratnavatī</s> addressed the frightened <s>Balabhadra</s>: "Do not be afraid. Say this: 'This is not <s>Kanakavatī</s>, the daughter of <s>Nidhipatidatta</s>. She is <s>Ratnavatī</s>, the daughter of <s>Gṛhagupta</s> from <s>Valabhī</s> itself, given to me by her parents and lawfully wedded. If you do not believe it, send an envoy to her kinsmen's side.'" And <s>Balabhadra</s>, having spoken thus, stood under the surety of the guild, until <s>Gṛhagupta</s>, having learned the true account from a letter [sent to] that city, came to <s>Kheṭaka</s> and, greatly delighted, took his daughter home together with his son-in-law. Having thus seen that <s>Ratnavatī</s> [was in truth] <s>Kanakavatī</s> [to him], <s>Balabhadra</s> — who had been imagining her to be <s>Kanakavatī</s> all along — became exceedingly fond of her. Therefore I say: "Desire (<s>Kāma</s>) is nothing but imagination (<s>saṅkalpa</s>)."'

bravīṣi ' iti paruṣam uktvā bahv atāḍayat | ceṭī tu prasāda-kāla-upakhyāta-rahasyasya vṛttānta-ekadeśam ātta-roṣā nirbibheda | tac chrutvā tu lubdhena daṇḍa-vāhinā paura-vṛddha-samnidhau ' nidhi-pati-dattasya kanyāṃ kanakavatīṃ moṣeṇa apahṛtya asmat-pure nivasaty eṣa dur-matir bala-bhadraḥ | tasya sarva-sva-haraṇaṃ bhavadbhir na pratibandhanīyam ' iti nitarām abhartsayata | bhītaṃ ca bala-bhadram adhijagāda ratnavatī -- ' na bhetavyam | brūhi -- na iyaṃ nidhi-pati-datta-kanyā kanakavatī | valabhyām eva gṛha-gupta-duhitā ratnavatī nāma iyaṃ dattā pitṛbhyāṃ mayā ca nyāyā uḍhā | na cet pratītha praṇidhiṃ prahiṇuta asyā bandhu-pārśvam ' iti | bala-bhadras tu tatha ūktvā śreṇī-prātibhāvyena tāvad eva atiṣṭhad yāvat tat-pura-lekhya-labdha-vṛttānto gṛha-guptaḥ kheṭaka-puram āgatya saha jāmātrā duhitaram ati-prītaḥ pratyanaiṣīt | tathā dṛṣṭvā ratnavatī kanakavati īti bhāvayatas tasya eva bhala-bhadrasya ati-vallabhā jātā | tad bravīmi -- ' kāmo nāma saṅkalpaḥ ' iti |

tadanantaram asau nitambavatīvṛttāntam aprākṣīt | so 'ham abravam - ' asti śūraseneṣu mathurā nāma nagarī | tatra kaś=cit kulaputraḥ kalāsu gaṇikāsu ca atiraktaḥ mitrārthaṃ svabhujamātranirvyūḍhānekakalahaḥ kalahakaṇṭaka iti karkaśair abhikhyāpitākhyaḥ pratyavātsīt | sa caikadā kasya=cid āgantoś citrakarasya haste citrapaṭaṃ dadarśa | tatra kā=cid ālekhyagatā yuvatir ālokamātreṇaiva kalahakaṇṭakasya kāmāturaṃ cetaś cakāra | sa ca tam abravīt - ' bhadra viruddham ivaitat pratibhāti | yataḥ kulajādurlabhaṃ vapuḥ ābhijātyaśamsinī ca namratā pāṇḍurā ca mukhacchaviḥ anatiparibhuktasubhagā ca tanuḥ prauḍhatānuviddhā ca dṛṣṭiḥ | na caiṣā proṣitabhartṛkā pravāsacihnasyaikaveṇīāder adarśanāt | lakṣma caitaddakṣiṇapārśvavarti | tad iyaṃ vṛddhasya kasya=cid vaṇijo na atipumstvasya yathārhasambhogā-lābhapīḍitā gṛhiṇī tvayā atikauśalād yathādṛṣṭam ālikhitā bhavitum arhati ' iti | sa tam abhipraśasya aśamsat - ' satyam idam | avantipuryām ujjayinyām anantakīrtināmnaḥ sārthavāhasya bhāryā yathārthanāmā nitambavatī nāmaiṣā saundaryavismitena mayaivam ālikhitā ' iti | sa tadaivonmanāyamānas taddarśanāya parivavrājojjayinīm | bhārgavo nāma bhūtvā bhikṣānibhena tadgṛhaṃ praviśya tāṃ dadarśa | dṛṣṭvā ca atyārūḍhamanmatho nirgatya pauramukhyebhyaḥ śmaśānarakṣām ayācata | alabhata ca | tatra labdhaiś ca śavāvaguṇṭhanapaṭādibhiḥ kām apy arhantikāṃ nāma śramaṇikām upāsāñ cakre | tanmukhena ca nimbavatīm upāmśu mantrayām āsa | sā caināṃ nirbhartsayantī pratyācacakṣe | śramaṇikāmukhāc ca duṣkaraśīlabhramśāṃ kulastriyam upalabhya rahasi dūtikām aśikṣayat - ' bhūyo 'py upatiṣṭha sārthavāhabhāryām | brūhi copahvare samsāradoṣadarśanāt samādhim āsthāya mumukṣamāṇo mādṛśo janaḥ kulavadhūnāṃ śīlapātane ghaṭatae iti kva ghaṭate | etad api tvam atyudārayā samṛddhyā rūpeṇa atimānuṣeṇa prathamena vayasopapannāṃ kim itaranārīsulabhaṃ cāpalaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ na veti parīkṣā kṛtā | tuṣṭā asmi tavaivam aduṣṭabhāvatayā | tvām idānīm utpannāpatyāṃ draṣṭum icchāmi | bhartā tu bhavatyāḥ kena=cid graheṇa adhiṣṭhitaḥ pāṇḍurogadurbalo bhoge ca asamarthaḥ sthito abhūt | na ca śakyaṃ tasya vighnam apratikṛtya apatyam asmāl labdhum | ataḥ prasīda | vṛkṣavāṭikām ekākinī praviśya madupanītasya kasya=cin mantravādinaś channam eva haste caraṇam arpayitvā tadabhimantritena praṇayakupitā nāma bhūtvā bhartāram urasi prahartum arhasi | upary asāv uttamadhātupuṣṭim ūrjitāpatyotpādanakṣamām āsādayiṣyati | anuvartiṣyate devīm iva atra bhavatīm | na atra śaṅkā kāryā iti | sā tathoktā vyaktam abhyupaiṣyati | naktaṃ māṃ vṛkṣavāṭikāṃ praveśya tām api praveśayiṣyasi | tāvataiva tvayā aham anugṛhīto bhave yam ' iti | sā tathaivopapāditavatī | so 'tiprītas tasyām eva kṣapāyāṃ vṛkṣavāṭikāṃ gato nitambavatīṃ nirgranthikāprayatnenopanītāṃ pāde parāmṛśann iva hemanūpuram ekam ākṣipya cchurikayorumūle kiñ=cid ālikhya drutataram apāsarat | sā tu sāndratrāsā svam eva durnayaṃ garhamāṇā jighāmsantīva śramaṇikāṃ tadvraṇaṃ bhavanadīrghikāyāṃ prakṣālya datvā paṭabandhanaṃ sāmayāpadeśād aparaṃ ca apanīya nūpuraṃ śayanaparā tricaturāṇi dināny ekānte ninye | sa dhūrtaḥ ' vikreṣye ' iti tena nūpureṇa tam anantakīrtim upāsasāda | sa dṛṣṭvā mama gṛhiṇyā evaiṣa nūpuraḥ katham ayam upalabdhas tvayā ' iti tam abruvāṇaṃ nirbandhena papraccha | sa tu ' vaṇiggrāmasya agre vakṣyāmi ' iti sthito abhūt | punar asau gṛhiṇyai ' svanūpurayugalaṃ preṣaya ' iti sandideśa | sā ca salajjaṃ sasādhvasaṃ ca ' adya rātrau viśrāmapraviṣṭāyāṃ vṛkṣavāṭikāyāṃ prabhraṣṭo mamaikaḥ praśithilabandho nūpuraḥ | so 'dya apy anviṣṭo na dṛṣṭaḥ | sa punar ayaṃ dvitīyaḥ ' ity aparaṃ prā hiṇot | anayā ca vārtayā amuṃ puraskṛtya sa vaṇig vaṇigjanasamājam ājagāma | sa ca anuyukto dhūrtaḥ savinayam āvedayat - ' viditam eva khalu vo yathā ahaṃ yuṣmadājñayā pitṛvanam abhi rakṣya tadupajīvī prativasāmi | lubdhāś ca kadā=cin maddarśanabhīravo niśi daheyur api śavānīti niśāsv api śmaśānam adhiśaye | aparedyur dagdhā-dagdhaṃ mṛtakaṃ citāyāḥ prasabham ākarṣantīṃ śyāmākārāṃ nārīm apaśyam | arthalobhāt tu nigṛhya bhayaṃ sā saṅgṛhītā | śastrikayorumūle yadṛcchayā kiñ=cid ullikhitam | eṣa ca nūpuraś caraṇād ākṣiptaḥ | tāvaty eva drutagatiḥ sā palāyiṣṭa | so 'yam asyāgamaḥ | paraṃ bhavantaḥ pramāṇam ' iti | vimarśe ca tasyāḥ śākinī tvam aikamatyena paurāṇām abhimatam āsīt | bhartrā ca parityaktā tasminn eva śmaśāne bahu vilapya pāśenodbadhya martukāmā tena dhūrtena naktam agṛhyata | anunītā ca - ' sundari tvadākāronmāditena mayā tvadāvarjane bahūn upāyān bhikṣukīmukhenopanyasya teṣv asiddheṣu punar ayam upāyo yāvajjīvam asādhāraṇīkṛtya rantum ācaritaḥ | tat prasīda ananyaśaraṇāya asmai dāsajanāya ' iti muhur muhuś caraṇayor nipatya prayujya sāntvaśatāni tām agatyantarām ātmavaśyām akarot | tad idam uktam - ' duṣkarasādhanaṃ prajñā ' iti |
children.translated_text: Thereupon he asked about the story of <s>Nitambavatī</s>. And I said: 'In the land of the <s>Śūrasenas</s>, there is a city called <s>Mathurā</s>. There lived a certain young man of good family, excessively attached to the arts and to courtesans, who had fought many quarrels single-handedly for the sake of friends, and who had been given the harsh epithet "<s>Kalahakaṇṭaka</s>" (the Thorn of Quarrel). One day he saw a painted scroll in the hand of a certain visiting painter. There, a certain young woman in the painting, by mere sight alone, set the passion-stricken mind of <s>Kalahakaṇṭaka</s> aflame. And he said to the painter: "Good sir, this seems contradictory. For her body is rare among women of good family, and her modesty bespeaks noble birth; her complexion is fair, her body not overly enjoyed yet still charming, and her gaze is tinged with maturity. Nor is she a woman whose husband is abroad, since there is no sign of it such as a single braid. And this beauty-mark is on the right side. Therefore, this must be the wife of some elderly merchant of no great virility, pained by the lack of proper enjoyment, and you, with great skill, must have painted her exactly as you saw her." The painter, praising him, confirmed: "This is true. In <s>Avantipurī</s> (<s>Ujjayinī</s>), she is the wife of a caravan-leader named <s>Anantakīrti</s>, and her name, aptly bestowed, is <s>Nitambavatī</s> (the Broad-Hipped One); amazed by her beauty, I have painted her thus." He, instantly becoming besotted, set out on foot for <s>Ujjayinī</s> to see her. Assuming the guise of a <s>Bhārgava</s> (mendicant <s>brāhmaṇa</s>), he entered her house under the pretext of begging alms and saw her. Having seen her, his passion utterly inflamed, he departed and begged from the city elders the post of guardian of the cremation ground, and obtained it. There, with the shrouds and cloths obtained from corpses, he cultivated some ascetic woman named <s>Arhantikā</s>. Through her, he secretly sent word to <s>Nitambavatī</s>. But she, rebuking the woman harshly, refused. And learning through the ascetic's mouth that the woman of good family was hard to seduce from virtue, he secretly instructed the go-between: "Approach the caravan-leader's wife again. And tell her in private: 'Does a person like me, who has attained meditative equanimity through seeing the faults of worldly existence and who desires liberation, engage in causing the fall of virtuous wives? Where is the question! Rather, since you are endowed with exceedingly generous prosperity, superhuman beauty, and the prime of youth—I tested whether the fickleness common in other women had touched you or not. I am pleased by your virtuous nature. Now I wish to see you when you have borne children. But your husband has been seized by some planetary affliction, is weakened by a bilious disease, and is incapable of sexual enjoyment. And it is not possible to obtain offspring from him without removing the affliction. Therefore, be gracious. Enter the garden alone, and secretly place your foot in the hand of a certain spell-caster brought by me. Having been empowered by his spell, pretending to be affectionately angry, you should strike your husband on the chest. Thereupon he will attain excellent constitutional vigor and become capable of producing noble offspring. He will attend upon you like a goddess. No doubt should be entertained in this matter.'" She, spoken to thus, will clearly consent. At night, you will bring me into the garden, and you will bring her in too. By that alone, you shall have done me a favor." She arranged it exactly so. Greatly delighted, on that very night he went to the garden, and while pretending to touch the foot of <s>Nitambavatī</s>—who had been brought by the ascetic's contrivance—he snatched one golden anklet, slightly scratched the base of her thigh with a small knife, and fled with great speed. She, in intense fright, blaming her own misconduct, wanting to kill the ascetic, washed that wound in the household pool, bandaged it, removed the other anklet too under the pretext of a vow, and spent three or four days in seclusion, intent on bed-rest. The rogue, saying 'I shall sell it,' approached <s>Anantakīrti</s> with that anklet. He, seeing it, said: 'This is the very anklet of my wife! How was it obtained by you?' and questioned him insistently. But the rogue stood firm, saying: 'I shall speak before the merchant guild.' Then <s>Anantakīrti</s> sent word to his wife: 'Send your pair of anklets.' And she, with embarrassment and trepidation, [thought]: 'Last night, when I entered the garden for rest, one of my loosely-fastened anklets fell off. Though searched for today, it was not found. And here is the second'—and sent the other one. And with this news, the merchant, putting the rogue forward, came to the merchant guild assembly. Questioned, the rogue reported respectfully: 'It is well known to you that, by your command, I guard the cemetery and live by its proceeds. Since thieves, fearing my sight, might sometimes burn even the corpses at night, I sleep in the cemetery even at night. On the following day, I saw a woman of dark form dragging a half-burnt corpse forcibly from the funeral pyre. Out of greed for gain, suppressing my fear, I seized her. With a small knife, the base of her thigh was accidentally scratched. And this anklet was snatched from her foot. With just that much, she fled at full speed. This is the account of its acquisition. But you, sirs, are the judges.' And in the deliberation, the opinion of the townsfolk was unanimous: 'She is a witch (<s>śākinī</s>).' Abandoned by her husband, she wept bitterly at that very cremation ground, and, wishing to die by hanging herself with a noose, she was seized at night by that rogue. And he placated her: 'Beautiful one! Maddened by your beauty, I devised many stratagems through the mouth of the mendicant woman for winning you over, and when those failed, I practiced this further device so as to enjoy you exclusively for life. Therefore, be gracious to this slave-person who has no other refuge.' Falling at her feet again and again and employing hundreds of soothing words, he brought her—who had no other recourse—under his sway. Hence it is said: "Intelligence is the means for accomplishing the difficult."'

sa cedam ākarṇya brahmarākṣaso mām apūpujat | asminn eva kṣaṇe na atiprauḍhapumnāgamukulasthūlāni muktāphalāni saha salilabindubhir ambaratalād apatan | ahaṃ tu ' kiṃ nv idam ' ity uccakṣur ālokayan kam=api rākṣasaṃ kāñ=cid aṅganāṃ viceṣṭamānagātrām ākarṣantam apaśyam | katham apaharaty akāmām api striyam anācāro nairṛta iti gaganagamanamandaśaktir aśastraś ca atapye | sa tu matsambandhī brahmarākṣasaḥ ' tiṣṭha tiṣṭha pāpa kva apaharasi ' iti bhartsayann utthāya rākṣasena sama sṛjyata | tāṃ tu roṣād anapekṣāpaviddhām amaravṛkṣamañjarīm iva antarikṣād āpatantīm unmukhaprasāritobhayakaraḥ karābhyām agrahīṣam | upagṛhya ca vepamānāṃ sammīlitākṣīṃ madaṅgasparśasukhenodbhinnaromāñcāṃ tādṛśīm eva tām anavatārayann atiṣṭham | tāvat tāv ubhāv api śailaśṛṅgabhaṅgaiḥ pādapaiś ca rabhasonmūlitair muṣṭipādaprahāraiś ca parasparam akṣapayetām | punar aham atimṛduni pulinavati kusumalavalāñchite sarastīre 'varopya saspṛhaṃ nirvarṇayams tāṃ matprāṇaikavallabhāṃ rājakanyāṃ kandukavatīm alakṣyam | sā hi mayā samāśvāsyamānā tiryaṅ mām abhinirūpya jātapratyabhijñā sakaruṇam arodīt | avādīc ca - ' nātha tvaddarśanād upoḍharāgā tasmin kandukotsave punaḥ sakhyā candrasenayā tvatkathābhir eva samāśvāsitā asmi | tvaṃ kila samudramadhye majjitaḥ pāpena madbhrātrā bhīmadhanvanā iti śrutvā sakhījanaṃ parijanaṃ ca vañcayitvā jīvitaṃ jihāsur ekākinī krīḍāvanam upāgamam | tatra ca mām acakamata kāmarūpa eṣa rākṣasādhamaḥ | so 'yaṃ mayā bhītayā avadhūtaprārthanaḥ sphurantīṃ māṃ nigṛhya abhyadhāvat | atraivam avasito 'bhūt | ahaṃ ca daivāt tavaiva jīvita īśasya haste patitā | bhadraṃ tava ' iti | śrutvā ca tayā saha avaruhya nāvam adhyāroham | muktā ca nauḥ prativātapreritā tām eva dāmaliptāṃ pratyupā tiṣṭhat | avarūḍhāś ca vayam aśrameṇa | ' tanayasya ca tanayāyāś ca nāśād ananyāpatyas tuṅgadhanvā suhmapatir niṣkalaḥ svayaṃ sakalatra eva niṣkalaṅkagaṅgārodhasy anaśanenoparantuṃ pratiṣṭhate | saha tena martum icchaty ananyanātho 'nuraktaḥ pauravṛddhalokaḥ | ' ity aśrumukhīnāṃ prajānām ākrandam aśṛṇuma | atha aham asmai rājñe yathāvṛttam ākhyāya tadapatyadvayaṃ pratyarpitavān | prītena tena jāmātā kṛto 'smi dāmalipteśvareṇa | tatputro madanujīvī jātaḥ | madājñaptena ca amunā prāṇavad ujjhitā candrasenā kośadāsam abhajat | tataś ca simhavarmasāhāyyārtham atrāgatya bhartus tava darśanotsavasukham anubhavāmi ' iti | śrutvā ' citreyaṃ daivagatiḥ | avasareṣu puṣkalaḥ puruṣakāraḥ | ' ity abhidhāya bhūyaḥ smitābhiṣiktadantacchado mantragupte harṣotphullaṃ cakṣuḥ pātayāmāsa devo rājavāhanaḥ | sa kila karakamalena kiñ=citsamvṛtānano lalitavallabhārabhasadattadantakṣatavyasanavihvalādharamaṇir niroṣṭhyavarṇam ātmacaritam ācacakṣe -
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the <s>Brahmarākṣasa</s> (brahmin-demon) honored me. At that very moment, pearls as large as the not-fully-opened buds of the male <s>nāga</s>-tree fell from the sky together with drops of water. But as I looked upward, wondering 'What is this?', I saw a certain <s>Rākṣasa</s> dragging a woman whose limbs were struggling. 'How can this vile <s>Nairṛta</s> (demon) abduct a woman against her will!' — I grieved, being only feebly capable of skyward flight and being without weapons. But the <s>Brahmarākṣasa</s> who was my kinsman, shouting 'Stop, stop, villain! Where are you taking her!', rose up and grappled with the <s>Rākṣasa</s>. The woman, in his fury hurled aside without regard — falling from the sky like a cluster of blossoms from the divine tree — I caught in both my upraised outstretched hands. Holding her as she trembled, her eyes shut, her hair standing on end from the pleasure of my touch, I stood there without setting her down, she being of such a condition. Meanwhile, those two shattered each other with mountain-peak fragments, uprooted trees, and blows of fists and feet, until both perished. Then I set her down on the exceedingly soft sandy bank of a lake, strewn with fallen flower-petals, and gazing at her with longing, I recognized that princess, the sole beloved of my life — <s>Kandukavatī</s>! And she, being comforted by me, looked at me sideways, recognized me, and wept with tender emotion. She said: 'Lord, from seeing you at that ball-game festival I was filled with love. Afterward, I was consoled by my friend <s>Candrasenā</s> with tales about you. When I heard that you had been drowned in the middle of the ocean by my wicked brother <s>Bhīmadhanvan</s>, I deceived my friends and attendants and, wishing to give up my life, went alone to the pleasure garden. There this lowest of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, able to assume any form at will, desired me. When I, frightened, rejected his advances, he seized me as I struggled and carried me off. And here it came to this. By fate, I have fallen into the very hands of you, the lord of my life. May it be well with you!' Having heard this, I descended with her and boarded a ship. The ship, released and driven by a favorable wind, arrived at that very <s>Dāmaliptā</s>. And we disembarked without difficulty. We heard the wailing of the people, their faces streaming with tears: 'Having lost both son and daughter, the childless lord of <s>Suhma</s>, <s>Tuṅgadhanvan</s>, with no other heir, though himself married, has set out to end his life by fasting on the bank of the stainless <s>Gaṅgā</s>. The devoted citizens, having no other protector, wish to die with him.' Then I explained all that had happened to this king and returned to him his two children. The delighted lord of <s>Dāmaliptā</s> made me his son-in-law. And his son, <s>Madanajīvī</s>, was born. At my command, <s>Candrasenā</s>, who had been abandoned as good as dead by him, took <s>Kośadāsa</s> as her husband. And from there, having come here to aid <s>Siṃhavarman</s>, I experience the festive happiness of beholding you, my lord.' Having heard this, the Lord <s>Rājavāhana</s> remarked: 'Wondrous is this course of fate! At opportune moments, human effort is abundant.' Then, his row of teeth anointed with a smile, he cast his gaze, blooming with delight, upon <s>Mantragupta</s>. He — slightly covering his face with his lotus-hand, his lower lip-gem trembling with the agitation caused by the teeth-marks passionately bestowed by his beloved <s>Lalitā</s> — began narrating his own story without labial consonants —

āpatantīm unmukha-prasārita-ubhaya-karaḥ karābhyām agrahīṣam | upagṛhya ca vepamānāṃ sammīlita-akṣīṃ mad-aṅga-sparśa-sukhena udbhinna-romāñcāṃ tādṛśīm eva tām an-avatārayann atiṣṭham | tāvat tāv ubhāv nirvarṇayams tāṃ mat-prāṇa-eka-vallabhāṃ rāja-kanyāṃ kandukavatīm alakṣyam | sā hi mayā samāśvāsyamānā tiryaṅ mām abhinirūpya jāta-pratyabhijñā sa-karuṇam arodīt | avādīc ca -- ' nātha tvad-darśanād upoḍha-rāgā tasmin kanduka-utsave punaḥ sakhyā candra-senayā tvat-kathābhir eva samāśvāsitā asmi | tvaṃ kila samudra-madhye majjitaḥ pāpena mad-bhrātrā bhīma-dhanvanā iti śrutvā sakhī-janaṃ parijanaṃ ca vañcayitvā jīvitaṃ jihāsur ekākinī krīḍā-vanam upāgamam | tatra ca mām acakamata kāma-rūpa eṣa rākṣasa-adhamaḥ | so 'yaṃ mayā bhītayā avadhūta-prārthanaḥ sphurantīṃ māṃ nigṛhya abhyadhāvat | atra pratyupā tiṣṭhat | avarūḍhāś ca vayam a-śrameṇa | ' tanayasya ca tanayāyāś ca nāśād an-anya-apatyas tuṅga-dhanvā suhma-patir niṣ-kalaḥ svayaṃ sa-kalatra eva niṣ-kalaṅka-gaṅgā-rodhasy an-aśanena uparantuṃ pratiṣṭhate | saha tena martum icchaty an-anya-nātho 'nuraktaḥ paura-vṛddha-lokaḥ | ' ity aśru-mukhīnāṃ prajānām ākrandam aśṛṇuma | atha aham asmai rājñe yathā-vṛttam ākhyāya tad-apatya-dvayaṃ pratyarpitavān | prītena tena jāmātā kṛto 'smi dāma-lipta-īśvareṇa | tat-putro mad-anujīvī jātaḥ | mad-ājñaptena ca amunā prāṇavad ujjhitā candra-senā kośa-dāsam abhajat | tataś ca simha-varma-sāhāyya-artham atrā agatya bhartus tava darśana-utsava-sukham anubhavāmi ' iti | śrutvā ' citra īyaṃ daiva-gatiḥ | avasareṣu puṣkalaḥ puruṣa-kāraḥ | ' ity abhidhāya bhūyaḥ smita-abhiṣikta-danta-cchado mantra-gupte harṣa-utphullaṃ cakṣuḥ pātayāmāsa devo rāja-vāhanaḥ | sa kila kara-kamalena kiñ=cit-samvṛta-ānano lalita-vallabhā-rabhasa-datta-danta-kṣata-vyasana-vihvala-adhara-maṇir nir-oṣṭhya-varṇam ātma-caritam ācacakṣe --
/ iti śrī daṇḍinaḥ kṛtau daśa-kumāra-carite mitra-gupta-caritaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭha ucchvāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter, called 'The Story of <s>Mitragupta</s>,' in the <s>Daśakumāracarita</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Daṇḍin</s>.
